title.zh: 卷426 列傳二百十三 王庆雲 谭廷襄 马新贻 李宗羲 徐宗幹 王凯泰 郭柏荫
title.en: Volume 426 Biographies 213: Wang Qingyun, Tan Tingxiang, Ma Xinyi, Li Zongxi, Xu Zonggan, Wang Kaitai, Guo Baiyin
title.raw: 卷426 列傳二百十三 王庆雲 谭廷襄 马新贻 李宗羲 徐宗幹 王凯泰 郭柏荫

sentences.zh: 王慶雲，字雁汀，福建閩縣人。

translations.literal: Wang Qingyun, style name Yanting, was a native of Min County, Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qingyun, whose style was Yanting, came from Min County in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 道光九年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Daoguang he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in 1829, entered the Hanlin Academy, and was made a compiler.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，大考一等，擢侍讀學士，遷通政副使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, in the grand examination he ranked first class and was promoted to reader-in-waiting of the Hanlin Academy, then transferred to vice commissioner of the Transmission Office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1847 he placed in the top class of the triennial Hanlin review and was promoted to reader-in-waiting, then made vice commissioner of the Transmission Office.

sentences.zh: 慶雲通知時事，尤究心財政，窮其利病，稽其出入。

translations.literal: Qingyun was well informed on current affairs and especially devoted himself to public finance, exhaustively studying its benefits and harms and tracing its receipts and disbursements.
translations.idiomatic: Qingyun kept abreast of current affairs and devoted himself above all to public finance, probing its strengths and weaknesses and tracking every inflow and outflow.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位求言，慶雲疏請通言路，省例案，寬民力，重國計。

translations.literal: When the Wenzong Emperor acceded and sought counsel, Qingyun memorialized asking to open channels of remonstrance, reduce routine paperwork, ease the people's burdens, and give weight to national accounts.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xianfeng Emperor came to the throne and called for counsel, Qingyun memorialized to open channels of remonstrance, cut routine paperwork, ease the people's burdens, and put national finance first.

sentences.zh: 其言重國計，略謂：「今歲入四千四五百萬，歲出在四千萬以下，田賦實徵近止二千八百萬。

translations.literal: On giving weight to national accounts, he said in summary: "Present annual revenue is forty-four or forty-five million, annual expenditure is under forty million, yet actual collection of land tax recently amounts to only about twenty-eight million.
translations.idiomatic: On strengthening the national accounts, he wrote in summary: "Annual revenue now runs to forty-four or forty-five million taels, while expenditure stays under forty million—yet actual land-tax collection lately barely reaches twenty-eight million.

sentences.zh: 夫旱潦事出偶然，而歲歲輪流請緩；

translations.literal: Drought and flood are matters of chance, yet year after year provinces take turns requesting deferral;
translations.idiomatic: Drought and flood are chance events, yet provinces take turns every year requesting tax deferrals;

sentences.zh: 鹽課歲額七百四十餘萬，實徵常不及五百萬。

translations.literal: The salt levy's annual quota is over seven million four hundred thousand, yet actual collection often falls short of five million.
translations.idiomatic: The salt levy is assessed at more than 7.4 million taels a year, yet collections often fail to reach five million.

sentences.zh: 生齒日增，而銷鹽日絀。

translations.literal: Population grows daily, yet salt sales daily fall short.
translations.idiomatic: The population grows daily, yet salt sales shrink by the day.

sentences.zh: 南河經費，嘉慶時止百餘萬，邇來遞增至三百五六十萬。

translations.literal: Southern River works funding under Jiaqing was only a little over a million; recently it has risen in stages to three million five or six hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Southern River works cost barely a million taels under Jiaqing; recently the figure has climbed in stages to 3.5 or 3.6 million.

sentences.zh: 入少出多，置之不問，思為一切苟且之計，何如取自有之財，詳細講求：地丁何以歲歲請緩？

translations.literal: Receipts are few and disbursements many, yet this is left unaddressed while one thinks of makeshift expedients—how much better to take the revenue already in hand and examine it in detail: why does land-and-poll tax request deferral year after year?
translations.idiomatic: Receipts lag behind spending, yet nothing is done except stopgap schemes—far better to take the revenue already at hand and study it closely: why is land-and-poll tax deferred year after year?

sentences.zh: 鹽課何以處處絀銷？

translations.literal: Why does the salt levy everywhere fall short in sales?
translations.idiomatic: Why does the salt levy fall short everywhere?

sentences.zh: 河工何以年年報險？

translations.literal: Why do river works report danger every year?
translations.idiomatic: Why do river works report emergencies every single year?

sentences.zh: 必得弊之所在而革除之。」

translations.literal: One must locate where the abuses lie and abolish them."
translations.idiomatic: The abuses must be found and rooted out."

sentences.zh: 奏入，上深韙焉。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor strongly approved it.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, the emperor strongly approved it.

sentences.zh: 時命中外大臣保薦人材，禮部侍郎曾國籓舉慶雲以應，詔擢詹事，署順天府尹。

translations.literal: At the time the court ordered civil and military officials to recommend talent; Vice Minister of Rites Zeng Guofan nominated Qingyun in response; an edict promoted him to grand tutor and made him acting metropolitan prefect of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: The court then ordered officials at court and in the provinces to recommend talent; Vice Minister of Rites Zeng Guofan nominated Qingyun, and an edict promoted him to grand tutor and acting metropolitan prefect of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，授戶部侍郎，仍署府尹。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he was appointed vice minister of Revenue and still acted as metropolitan prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In 1851 he was appointed vice minister of Revenue while continuing to act as metropolitan prefect.

sentences.zh: 內務府議令莊頭增租，佃戶不應，則勒限退地。

translations.literal: The Imperial Household Department proposed ordering estate managers to raise rents; when tenants refused, they would be forced within a deadline to surrender the land.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Household Department proposed ordering estate managers to raise rents; if tenants refused, they would be forced to surrender the land within a set deadline.

sentences.zh: 慶雲偕直隸總督訥爾經額援乾隆間停設莊頭，嘉慶間奏禁增租奪佃兩案，奏請敕內務府不得任意加租。

translations.literal: Qingyun together with Zhili governor-general Ne'erjing'e cited the Qianlong-era case abolishing estate managers and the Jiaqing-era memorials forbidding rent increases and dispossession of tenants, and memorialized requesting an edict that the Imperial Household Department must not raise rents at will.
translations.idiomatic: Qingyun joined Zhili governor-general Ne'erjing'e in citing Qianlong precedents abolishing estate managers and Jiaqing bans on rent hikes and tenant dispossession, and memorialized for an edict forbidding the Imperial Household Department to raise rents arbitrarily.

sentences.zh: 戶部請改河東鹽政章程，並清查山西州縣虧空，命慶雲偕浙江布政使聯英往按。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue requested reform of the Hedong salt administration regulations and an audit of deficits in Shanxi prefectures and counties; Qingyun was ordered to go with Zhejiang provincial treasurer Lian Ying to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue sought reform of Hedong salt regulations and an audit of Shanxi fiscal deficits; Qingyun was sent with Zhejiang provincial treasurer Lian Ying to investigate.

sentences.zh: 尋奏定清查虧空章程，並會山西巡撫那蘇圖奏言：「晉商賠累，一在鹽本鉅，一在浮費多，一在運腳重。

translations.literal: Soon he memorialized fixing regulations for auditing deficits, and jointly with Shanxi governor Naxutu memorialized saying: "Shanxi merchants' losses stem first from the great cost of salt capital, second from numerous extraneous fees, third from heavy transport charges.
translations.idiomatic: He soon fixed regulations for auditing deficits and, with Shanxi governor Naxutu, reported: "Shanxi merchants' losses come first from heavy salt capital costs, second from excessive overhead, third from crushing transport charges.

sentences.zh: 官鹽既貴，私販遂乘間蔓延。

translations.literal: Once government salt grew costly, private traders took advantage of the gap and spread.
translations.idiomatic: As official salt grew costly, smugglers seized the opening and spread everywhere.

sentences.zh: 從前鹽價每石三五十兩，自坐商囤積居奇，畦地錠票，租典靡常，一業數主，人人牟利。

translations.literal: Formerly salt was thirty or fifty taels per picul; since resident merchants hoarded and held prices up, salt-field deeds and tally tickets changed hands constantly, one trade had many masters, and each sought profit.
translations.idiomatic: Salt once sold for thirty or fifty taels a picul; resident merchants then hoarded stock and rigged prices, salt-field deeds and tally tickets changed hands endlessly, and every link in the trade took its cut.

sentences.zh: 一石之鹽，貴百三四十兩，運商安得不困？

translations.literal: One picul of salt cost one hundred thirty or forty taels—how could transport merchants not be distressed?
translations.idiomatic: A single picul cost 130 or 140 taels—small wonder transport merchants were ruined.

sentences.zh: 河東鹽行三省，酬應繁多，總商分派者號為廳攤，散商自送者歲有常例，統計二十六萬餘兩，幾達歲課之半。

translations.literal: Hedong salt served three provinces; entertainments were numerous; what the chief merchant apportioned was called hall assessments, what petty merchants delivered on their own had annual customary fees—in all over 260,000 taels, nearly half the annual levy.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong salt served three provinces with endless hospitality costs; chief merchants' apportioned "hall assessments" and petty merchants' customary gifts totaled more than 260,000 taels—nearly half the annual levy.

sentences.zh: 加以石鹽腳費多至百兩，因其定價難增，遂至相率為偽，攙沙短秤，民食愈艱。

translations.literal: Added to this, transport charges per picul often reached a hundred taels; because fixed prices could hardly rise, all turned to fraud—mixing sand and shorting scales—so the people's salt grew ever harder to obtain.
translations.idiomatic: Transport charges per picul often hit a hundred taels; with official prices frozen, merchants adulterated salt and shorted weights, and the people's supply grew ever scarcer.

sentences.zh: 臣等公同商酌，輕鹽本必先定池價，革浮費必先行​​票法，減運腳必先分口岸，將緝私之法並寓其中。

translations.literal: We have jointly deliberated: to lighten salt capital one must first fix pond prices; to cut extraneous fees one must first institute the tally system; to reduce transport charges one must first divide ports—and anti-smuggling measures are to be embodied in all of this.
translations.idiomatic: We agreed that lowering salt capital requires fixing pond prices first; cutting overhead requires the tally system first; reducing transport costs requires dividing ports first—with anti-smuggling built into each step.

sentences.zh: 蓋鹽有專商，票無定販，大要在留商招販，先課后鹽，而後引目不致虛懸，課額無虞短絀。

translations.literal: Salt has exclusive merchants but tallies have no fixed traffickers; the main point is to retain merchants to recruit traders, levy duty before salt, so that quotas are not left vacant and revenue is not short.
translations.idiomatic: Salt has licensed merchants but tallies need not bind fixed traders; the key is to keep merchants recruiting buyers, collect duty before salt moves, and keep quotas filled so revenue does not fall short.

sentences.zh: 向來坐商昂價，總以缺產為詞。

translations.literal: Resident merchants have always raised prices, always citing short supply.
translations.idiomatic: Resident merchants have always raised prices, always pleading short supply.

sentences.zh: 臣覽池面寬廣，滷氣醲厚，即雨暘不齊，裒多益寡，足敷五千六百餘石之額。

translations.literal: I have viewed the ponds—they are broad, the brine rich and thick; even if rain and drought are uneven, pooling surplus to cover shortage suffices for the quota of over 5,600 piculs.
translations.idiomatic: The ponds are broad and the brine rich; even in uneven weather, pooling surplus to cover shortage can meet the quota of more than 5,600 piculs.

sentences.zh: 鹽貴不在缺產，而在售私。

translations.literal: Salt is costly not from short supply but from selling private salt.
translations.idiomatic: Salt is costly not from short supply but from smuggling.

sentences.zh: 擬定白鹽一石貴止六十兩，青鹽遞減，坐商工本外有贏餘。

translations.literal: It is proposed to fix white salt at no more than sixty taels per picul, with green salt reduced stepwise, so resident merchants have surplus beyond production costs.
translations.idiomatic: We propose capping white salt at sixty taels a picul, with green salt priced lower in steps, leaving resident merchants a margin above production cost.

sentences.zh: 令各商立法互稽，但使鹽不旁流，商鹽自富，錠票銷價，亦復刪芟。

translations.literal: Let each merchant establish rules for mutual inspection; so long as salt does not flow sideways, merchant salt will enrich itself, and tally resale prices will also be pruned.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants should set mutual inspection rules; if salt does not leak sideways, licensed trade will prosper and tally resale prices can be cut back.

sentences.zh: 畦地租典，先侭運商，總期減輕成本，禁衛課官吏浮費，別籌公用。

translations.literal: Salt-field leases should go first to transport merchants, all aiming to lighten costs; forbid extraneous fees by revenue guards and clerks, and provide for public expenses separately.
translations.idiomatic: Salt-field leases should go first to transport merchants to cut costs; extraneous fees by revenue guards and clerks must be banned and public expenses funded separately.

sentences.zh: 每票徵銀七分有奇，隨課收發，此外需索，坐贓科罪。

translations.literal: Each tally is to levy a little over seven fen of silver, issued and collected with the duty; any further demands are to be punished as embezzlement.
translations.idiomatic: Each tally should levy just over seven fen of silver, collected with the duty; any further demands will be treated as embezzlement.

sentences.zh: 其領票、招販、掣鹽、截角諸事，悉仿兩淮成例，微為變通，以歸簡易。

translations.literal: Receiving tallies, recruiting traders, drawing salt, and cutting corner vouchers—all are to follow Liang-Huai precedents with slight adaptation for simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: Issuing tallies, recruiting traders, drawing salt, and cutting transport vouchers should follow Liang-Huai practice with slight local adjustments for simplicity.

sentences.zh: 河東鹽行河南引地，自嘉慶二十四年改為商運民銷，以會興鎮為發鹽口岸，商民稱便。

translations.literal: Hedong salt in Henan's quota area, since the twenty-fourth year of Jiaqing, was changed to merchant transport and popular sale, with Huixing Town as the salt issue port—merchants and people called it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Since Jiaqing 24, Hedong salt in Henan has been merchant-transported and retailed locally, with Huixing Town as the issue port—a arrangement merchants and people welcomed.

sentences.zh: 擬將陝西、山西、會興鎮分為三路，不許攙越，鹽到發販隨銷，亦聽商人自運，兼防夾私，力杜作偽。

translations.literal: It is proposed to divide Shaanxi, Shanxi, and Huixing Town into three routes, forbidding cross-over; salt arrives and is sold as distributed, merchants may also transport on their own, while guarding against smuggling and firmly stopping fraud.
translations.idiomatic: We propose three routes for Shaanxi, Shanxi, and Huixing Town with no cross-traffic; salt is sold where it arrives, merchants may self-transport, smuggling is checked, and fraud is stamped out.

sentences.zh: 統計河東全綱，比較昔價，裁浮改岸，年省七十餘萬。

translations.literal: Counting the whole Hedong salt quota, compared with former prices, cutting overhead and changing ports saves over 700,000 taels yearly.
translations.idiomatic: For the whole Hedong quota, trimming overhead and changing ports against former prices would save more than 700,000 taels a year.

sentences.zh: 得人守法，商力不疲。

translations.literal: With the right men enforcing the law, merchant strength will not be exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: With capable men enforcing the rules, merchants will not be ruined.

sentences.zh: 即間有歇業，或運商歸併，或坐商承充，永絕舉商、保商諸弊。」

translations.literal: Even if some cease business, transport merchants may merge or resident merchants may fill vacancies, forever ending the abuses of nominating merchants and guarantor merchants."
translations.idiomatic: If some firms quit, transport merchants may merge or resident merchants fill in—ending forever the abuses of brokered nominations and guarantor merchants."

sentences.zh: 下部議行。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries deliberated and adopted it.

sentences.zh: 慶雲既明習計政，主部事，先後奏請清釐江寧、蘇州、安徽三布政司例應入撥、延未造報各款，自道光三年至咸豐元年，凡千五十九款，九百三十六萬兩。

translations.literal: Qingyun, now well versed in fiscal administration and directing ministry affairs, successively memorialized to clear items that the Jiangning, Suzhou, and Anhui provincial treasuries should have entered into transfers but had long failed to report—from the third year of Daoguang to the first year of Xianfeng, 1,059 items in all, 9.36 million taels.
translations.idiomatic: Now expert in fiscal affairs and directing the ministry, Qingyun cleared 1,059 transfer items totaling 9.36 million taels that Jiangning, Suzhou, and Anhui treasuries should have reported from 1823 to 1851 but had long left outstanding.

sentences.zh: 又奏言：「江南賦甲他省，額徵五百二十九萬，道光十六年，豁欠五百六十餘萬，計十年蠲一年之額；

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Jiangnan's levies rank first among provinces, with a quota of 5.29 million; in the sixteenth year of Daoguang, over 5.6 million in arrears was remitted—amounting in ten years to remitting one year's quota;
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Jiangnan's tax quota leads all provinces at 5.29 million taels; in 1836 over 5.6 million in arrears was written off—effectively remitting one year's levy every ten years;

sentences.zh: 二十六年，豁欠一千餘萬，計十年蠲兩年。

translations.literal: in the twenty-sixth year, over ten million in arrears was remitted—amounting in ten years to remitting two years.
translations.idiomatic: in 1846 over ten million was written off—two years' quota every decade.

sentences.zh: 及咸豐二年，豁欠一千三百餘萬，十年幾蠲三年。

translations.literal: by the second year of Xianfeng, over thirteen million was remitted—in ten years nearly three years' quota.
translations.idiomatic: By 1852 over thirteen million was written off—nearly three years' quota every decade.

sentences.zh: 請飭江蘇督撫，熟田未完，不得混入次年緩徵。」

translations.literal: He asked that Jiangsu governor-general and governor be ordered: arrears on mature fields must not be mixed into the next year's deferred collection."
translations.idiomatic: He asked the Jiangsu authorities to forbid mixing mature-field arrears into the next year's deferred collections."

sentences.zh: 又奏覆閩浙總督季芝昌等以閩鹺疲累，請展緩勻代額課，言：「閩鹺所以疲累，病在私鹽充斥，浮費繁重。

translations.literal: He also replied to Fujian-Zhejiang governor-general Ji Zhichang and others, who because Fujian salt was exhausted requested extension, deferral, and averaged substitution of the quota levy, saying: "Fujian salt is exhausted because private salt fills the market and extraneous fees are heavy.
translations.idiomatic: He also replied to Fujian-Zhejiang governor-general Ji Zhichang's plea to defer and average Fujian's salt quota: "Fujian salt fails because smuggling is rampant and overhead is crushing.

sentences.zh: 芝昌等議停勻代課六萬餘，派認續例課二萬餘，五年之後，勻代起徵，例課仍納。

translations.literal: Ji Zhichang and others proposed suspending the averaged substitution levy of over 60,000, assigning continued customary levy of over 20,000, and after five years resuming averaged substitution while still paying the customary levy.
translations.idiomatic: Ji proposed suspending 60,000 taels of averaged quota, assigning 20,000 in continuing customary levy, then resuming the average after five years while still paying the customary levy.

sentences.zh: 朝三暮四，恐無此辦法。」

translations.literal: Morning three, evening four—there is probably no such method."
translations.idiomatic: This morning-three-evening-four scheme is hardly workable."

sentences.zh: 又言：「芝昌等但陳料理之難，未籌補救之法，或就場徵課，或按包抽稅。

translations.literal: He also said: "Ji Zhichang and others only stated the difficulty of handling matters and did not plan remedies—either levy at the salt works or tax by bundle.
translations.idiomatic: He added that Ji had only described difficulties, not remedies—either levy at the works or tax by bundle.

sentences.zh: 應令擇一可行之策，另議具奏。」

translations.literal: They should be ordered to choose one workable plan and memorialize separately in detail."
translations.idiomatic: They should pick one workable plan and submit a detailed memorial."

sentences.zh: 又奏覆江西巡撫張芾請撥粵鹽濟銷，言：「江西借撥粵鹽，前明總制陳南金、巡撫王守仁嘗行之，所謂不加賦而財足，不擾民而事辦，其法至善。

translations.literal: He also replied to Jiangxi governor Zhang Fu's request to allocate Guangdong salt for relief sales, saying: "Jiangxi borrowing Guangdong salt was once done by Ming grand coordinator Chen Nanjin and governor Wang Shouren—what is called enriching the treasury without raising levies and accomplishing affairs without troubling the people; the method is excellent.
translations.idiomatic: He also endorsed Jiangxi governor Zhang Fu's request to allocate Guangdong salt, citing Ming precedents of Chen Nanjin and Wang Shouren—"enriching revenue without new levies, accomplishing the task without troubling the people"—as an excellent policy.

sentences.zh: 應令速籌遵辦。」

translations.literal: They should be ordered to plan quickly and comply."
translations.idiomatic: They should arrange it at once."

sentences.zh: 又奏：「滇、黔解運銅鉛，道遠阻兵。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Yunnan and Guizhou forwarding copper and lead, the route is long and blocked by warfare.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote that Yunnan and Guizhou could no longer forward copper and lead—the routes were long and blocked by war.

sentences.zh: 應令於提鎮駐紮重兵之處，籌鑄制錢，並於附近水次兼鑄大錢，運四川、兩湖易銀，並派民間交納地丁稅課。」

translations.literal: They should be ordered at places where provincial commanders and brigadiers station heavy troops to arrange casting of standard cash, and at nearby waterways also cast large cash, transport to Sichuan and the two Hu basins to exchange for silver, and assign the populace to pay land-and-poll tax in them."
translations.idiomatic: Standard cash should be cast where major garrisons stand, large cash at nearby waterways, then shipped to Sichuan and the two Hu provinces to exchange for silver and accept land-and-poll tax payments."

sentences.zh: 又奏：「新疆南、北兩路駐兵四萬，歲需經費一百三四十萬，垂及百年，為數万萬。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Xinjiang's southern and northern routes station 40,000 troops, needing 1.3 or 1.4 million yearly; approaching a century, the sum is tens of millions.
translations.idiomatic: He also noted that 40,000 troops on Xinjiang's northern and southern routes cost 1.3–1.4 million taels a year—tens of millions over nearly a century.

sentences.zh: 請停陝省官兵換防喀什噶爾等八城，即由伊犁、烏魯木齊滿、綠營飭撥，五年更換，可歲省數十萬。」

translations.literal: He asked to stop Shaanxi troops rotating garrison duty at Kashgar and the other eight cities, and instead detail Manchu and Green Standard troops from Ili and Urumqi on five-year rotations, saving hundreds of thousands yearly."
translations.idiomatic: He proposed ending Shaanxi troop rotations to Kashgar and the eight cities, using Ili and Urumqi Manchu and Green Standard garrisons on five-year turns instead—saving hundreds of thousands a year."

sentences.zh: 又奏請裁東河河督南河河庫道併兩河廳員修防經費，南河不得過百萬，東河不得過七八十萬，並裁漕督，歸南河總督兼管。

translations.literal: He also memorialized requesting abolition of the Eastern River director, Southern River treasury intendant, and merger of staff on both rivers; repair funds for the Southern River not to exceed one million, Eastern River not to exceed seven or eight hundred thousand; and abolition of the grain transport director, merged under the Southern River governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: He also sought to abolish the Eastern and Southern River directorships, merge river offices, cap Southern River repairs at one million and Eastern at 700–800,000 taels, and fold the grain-transport directorate into the Southern River governor-general's portfolio.

sentences.zh: 各疏多如所議行。

translations.literal: Most of these memorials were adopted as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: Most of these proposals were adopted.

sentences.zh: 尋授陝西巡撫。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed governor of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed governor of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 四年，粵匪擾河南，慶雲赴潼關，與提督丰紳、將軍扎拉芬籌防禦。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Cantonese rebels disturbed Henan; Qingyun went to Tong Pass and with provincial commander Feng Shen and general Zhala Fen planned defense.
translations.idiomatic: In 1854, when Taiping forces threatened Henan, Qingyun went to Tong Pass to plan defenses with commander Feng Shen and general Zhala Fen.

sentences.zh: 又自潼關赴商南，遍歷各隘。

translations.literal: He also went from Tong Pass to Shangnan and inspected every pass.
translations.idiomatic: He then traveled from Tong Pass to Shangnan and inspected every mountain pass.

sentences.zh: 上命丰紳率兵駐襄陽。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Feng Shen to lead troops and garrison Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Feng Shen to garrison Xiangyang with his troops.

sentences.zh: 粵匪陷武昌，慶雲請以湖北會城暫移襄陽，山西、四川協籌軍餉，保全大局。

translations.literal: When Cantonese rebels took Wuchang, Qingyun asked that Hubei's provincial seat be temporarily moved to Xiangyang, with Shanxi and Sichuan jointly raising military funds to preserve the overall situation.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels took Wuchang, Qingyun urged moving Hubei's capital temporarily to Xiangyang and having Shanxi and Sichuan help fund the army to hold the line.

sentences.zh: 尋調山西巡撫。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to governor of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to governor of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 五年，奏言：「潞鹽行銷山西、陝西、河南三省，陝患鹽多，晉苦值貴。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he memorialized: "Lu salt is marketed in Shanxi, Shaanxi, and Henan; Shaanxi suffers from too much salt, Jin suffers from high prices.
translations.idiomatic: In 1855 he reported that Lu salt served Shanxi, Shaanxi, and Henan—Shaanxi was flooded with salt while Shanxi groaned under high prices.

sentences.zh: 擬將陝引勻銷晉省三百七十石。

translations.literal: It is proposed to average 370 piculs of Shaanxi quota sales into Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed averaging 370 piculs of Shaanxi quota into Shanxi sales.

sentences.zh: 晉引則就地遠近，公平定價。

translations.literal: For Jin quota, prices are to be set fairly according to local distance.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxi quota prices would be set fairly by distance from source.

sentences.zh: 惟河南官運已覺暢行，擬兼行民運，以廣招徠。

translations.literal: Henan's official transport already runs smoothly; it is proposed also to allow popular transport to broaden recruitment.
translations.idiomatic: Henan's official transport was working well; he proposed adding private transport to widen participation.

sentences.zh: 禁止吉蘭泰、花馬池鹽侵銷。」

translations.literal: Forbid Jilantai and Huamachi salt from encroaching on sales."
translations.idiomatic: Smuggled salt from Jilantai and Huamachi was to be barred from the market."

sentences.zh: 又言：「陝省課歸地丁，輸納不前，請仿河南招販民運，於河東、河西擇地設局稽查。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Shaanxi's levy is merged into land-and-poll tax and payment lags; please follow Henan in recruiting traders for popular transport and establish inspection bureaus on the east and west of the river."
translations.idiomatic: He also urged that because Shaanxi's salt levy was folded into land tax and payments lagged, the province should follow Henan's trader-recruitment model and set up inspection offices east and west of the Yellow River."

sentences.zh: 又奏言：「軍興以來，各軍營用銀出納，易錢買糧，歲豐銀裕，何便如之！

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Since warfare began, camps disburse silver, exchange cash for grain—in a bountiful year with ample silver, what could be more convenient!
translations.idiomatic: He also noted that since the war began armies paid in silver and bought grain with cash—in good harvest years with ample silver, nothing could be more convenient.

sentences.zh: 今用兵之地，賦稅不全，仰給鄰省，完善之區，正供不足，佐以捐輸。

translations.literal: Now in war zones taxes are incomplete and they rely on neighboring provinces; in intact regions regular revenue is insufficient and donations supplement it.
translations.idiomatic: Now war zones cannot collect full taxes and depend on neighbors; intact regions cannot meet regular quotas and rely on donations.

sentences.zh: 當此穀貴錢荒，以銀易錢，以錢易糧，耗折大半。

translations.literal: At this time of costly grain and scarce cash, exchanging silver for cash and cash for grain wastes more than half.
translations.idiomatic: With grain dear and cash scarce, converting silver to cash and cash to grain wastes more than half the value.

sentences.zh: 往時兵飢，得銀可飽，恐此後以銀亦不可飽，況銀且不可常繼。

translations.literal: Formerly when troops were hungry, receiving silver could fill them; I fear hereafter silver may not fill them either—and moreover silver cannot be sustained constantly.
translations.idiomatic: Once hungry soldiers could be fed with silver; soon even silver may not feed them—and silver cannot be relied on indefinitely.

sentences.zh: 擬令州縣碾動倉穀，解餉兼用制錢，舟楫可通，宜無不便。」

translations.literal: It is proposed to order prefectures and counties to mill granary grain, deliver rations, and also use standard cash; where boats can pass, there should be no inconvenience."
translations.idiomatic: He proposed having counties mill granary grain for rations and using standard cash as well—where waterways allowed, both should work."

sentences.zh: 均如所請。

translations.literal: All were granted as requested.
translations.idiomatic: All were approved.

sentences.zh: 又奏：「山西前明逼近三邊郡縣，率民築堡自衛。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "In Shanxi under the former Ming, counties near the Three Borders led the people to build forts for self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: He also reported that in Ming times Shanxi border counties had led people to build fortified villages for self-defense.

sentences.zh: 一縣十餘堡至百數十堡，星羅釭布。

translations.literal: One county had over ten forts to over a hundred or several tens, scattered like stars and set like nails.
translations.idiomatic: A single county might have from a dozen to over a hundred forts, scattered like stars across the landscape.

sentences.zh: 今惟云中、代、朔，堡寨相連，省南各屬，則多殘缺，當令繕完。

translations.literal: Today only Yunzhong, Dai, and Shuo have forts and stockades linked; in the southern parts of the province many are ruined and should be ordered repaired.
translations.idiomatic: Today only Yunzhong, Dai, and Shuo still have linked fort networks; southern prefectures' forts are mostly ruined and should be repaired.

sentences.zh: 定社規，立義學，化導少壯惰遊，合祭賽以聯其情，相守望以齊其力。

translations.literal: Fix community rules, establish charity schools, reform idle youth, unite festival sacrifices to bind feelings, and watch for one another to align strength.
translations.idiomatic: Community rules and charity schools should reform idle youth; joint festivals would bind neighbors together and mutual watch would align their strength.

sentences.zh: 有事則聚守，無事則散居，於無形中寓堅壁清野之法。」

translations.literal: When trouble comes they gather to defend; when calm they scatter to dwell—invisibly embodying the method of fortified villages and cleared countryside."
translations.idiomatic: In danger they would gather inside; in peace they would farm outside—applying fortified-village and scorched-country tactics without saying so."

sentences.zh: 又以河南南陽諸地旱蝗，請飭發倉籌賑，俾災民不為土匪勾脅，以救災即以弭患。

translations.literal: He also, because Nanyang and other places in Henan suffered drought and locusts, asked that granaries be opened for relief so disaster victims would not be seduced by bandits—relieving disaster is itself quelling trouble.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged opening granaries for drought and locust victims in Nanyang and elsewhere in Henan so they would not join bandits—relief itself would prevent unrest.

sentences.zh: 捻匪擾南陽，慶雲密陳省南分三路，遣兵巡防。

translations.literal: Nian rebels disturbed Nanyang; Qingyun secretly reported dividing the south of the province into three routes and dispatching troops to patrol.
translations.idiomatic: When Nian rebels threatened Nanyang, Qingyun privately proposed dividing southern Shanxi into three routes for patrol troops.

sentences.zh: 擢四川總督，貴州思南教匪為亂，慶雲遣兵防酉陽秀山，請飭總兵蔣玉龍自鎮遠規复思南。

translations.literal: He was promoted to governor-general of Sichuan; when teaching-bandit rebels rose in Sinan, Guizhou, Qingyun sent troops to guard Youyang and Xiushan and asked that brigade general Jiang Yulong advance from Zhenyuan to recover Sinan.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Sichuan governor-general, he sent troops to guard Youyang and Xiushan when sect rebels rose in Guizhou's Sinan and asked brigade general Jiang Yulong to advance from Zhenyuan to retake the city.

sentences.zh: 尋奏四川舊有啯匪，盜案多於他省，飭各屬行保甲，立限捕盜。

translations.literal: Soon he memorialized that Sichuan had long had Gua bandits and theft cases exceeded other provinces; he ordered all jurisdictions to implement baojia and set deadlines for catching thieves.
translations.idiomatic: He soon reported that Sichuan's long-standing Gua bandits made theft cases exceed other provinces and ordered baojia enforcement with deadlines for arrests.

sentences.zh: 又奏於酉陽設屯田，分設屯兵駐防城鄉要隘。

translations.literal: He also memorialized establishing garrison farms at Youyang and posting garrison troops at urban and rural strategic points.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed garrison farms at Youyang and posting troops at key towns and passes.

sentences.zh: 又奏：「川省差役捕盜，傳證起贓，輒糾多人，持械搜掠，名曰'掃通'者，此與強盜無異。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "In Sichuan when yamen runners catch thieves and summon witnesses to recover stolen goods, they often muster many men, seize weapons, and search and plunder—what is called 'sao tong'—this is no different from armed robbery.
translations.idiomatic: He also condemned Sichuan runners who, while recovering stolen goods, mustered armed gangs to search and loot households in so-called "sao tong" raids—no different from robbery.

sentences.zh: 請照強盜律，不分首從皆斬，兵丁有犯同之。」

translations.literal: He asked that under the armed-robbery statute, leaders and followers alike be beheaded, and soldiers who commit the same be treated equally."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that all participants be beheaded under the armed-robbery statute, soldiers included."

sentences.zh: 均下部議行。

translations.literal: All were sent to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries adopted them all.

sentences.zh: 尋以黔匪焚掠，漸近綦南，遣兵出境攻層巒山、飛梯岩諸隘，又破胡家坪賊巢。

translations.literal: Soon because Guizhou rebels burned and plundered and gradually neared Qinan, he sent troops across the border to attack passes at Cengluan Mountain and Feiti Cliff, and also broke the rebel nest at Hujiaping.
translations.idiomatic: When Guizhou rebels burned and looted their way toward Qinan, he sent troops across the border to take Cengluan Mountain and Feiti Cliff passes and destroy the nest at Hujiaping.

sentences.zh: 九年，兼署成都將軍，調兩廣總督。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he also acted as Chengdu general and was transferred to governor-general of Liang-Guang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1859 he also acted as Chengdu general and was transferred to governor-general of the two Guang provinces.

sentences.zh: 行次漢陽，以病乞罷，許之。

translations.literal: En route he stopped at Hanyang, begged leave on grounds of illness, and was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: En route he fell ill at Hanyang, asked to resign, and was allowed to do so.

sentences.zh: 旋召詣京師，病未即行。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned to the capital but did not go at once because of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon summoned to Beijing but illness kept him from going immediately.

sentences.zh: 十一年，穆宗即位，授左都御史，擢工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, when the Muzong Emperor acceded, he was appointed left censor-in-chief and promoted to minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In 1861, when the Tongzhi Emperor acceded, he was made left censor-in-chief and then minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 同治元年三月，慶雲將力疾赴召，前一日劇病，卒，諡文勤。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Tongzhi, Qingyun was about to go to court despite illness; the day before he fell gravely ill and died; his posthumous name was Wenqin.
translations.idiomatic: In March 1862, as Qingyun prepared to answer the summons despite his illness, he took a sudden turn for the worse and died; he was posthumously named Wenqin.

sentences.zh: 孫仁堪，循吏有傳。

translations.literal: His grandson Sun Renkan has a separate biography as an exemplary local official.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Sun Renkan has his own biography among the model local officials.

sentences.zh: 譚廷襄，字竹厓，浙江山陰人。

translations.literal: Tan Tingxiang, style name Zhuya, was a native of Shanyin, Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Tingxiang, whose style was Zhuya, came from Shanyin in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 道光十三年進士，選庶吉士，散館授刑部主事，再遷郎中。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Daoguang he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, on leaving the Academy was appointed a principal secretary in the Ministry of Punishments, and was later promoted to director.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi in 1833, entered the Hanlin Academy, and on leaving was made a secretary in the Ministry of Punishments, later promoted to director.

sentences.zh: 出為直隸永平知府，調保定，遷順天府尹，擢刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: He went out as prefect of Yongping in Zhili, was transferred to Baoding, promoted to metropolitan prefect of Shuntian, and elevated to vice minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Yongping in Zhili, transferred to Baoding, became Shuntian metropolitan prefect, and was promoted to vice minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 咸豐六年，出為陝西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xianfeng he went out as governor of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1856 he was appointed governor of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 直省採米運京倉，廷襄疏言：「陝西產米少，轉輸不便。

translations.literal: Provinces collected grain and shipped it to the capital granaries; Tingxiang memorialized: "Shaanxi produces little rice and transport is inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: When provinces were to ship grain to Beijing, Tingxiang wrote: "Shaanxi produces little rice, and transport is impractical.

sentences.zh: 請改折解款，由部召糴，費節而事集。」

translations.literal: He asked to convert to monetary payment, with the ministry purchasing grain—saving expense while accomplishing the task."
translations.idiomatic: He asked to pay in silver instead, with the ministry buying grain—cheaper and more efficient."

sentences.zh: 七年，署直隸總督。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he acted as Zhili governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: In 1857 he acted as Zhili governor-general.

sentences.zh: 是時英、法、俄、美四國合軍陷廣東省城，廷襄疏請封貨閉關，恩威並用，上以海運在途，激之生變，虛聲無實益，不允。

translations.literal: At that time the combined armies of Britain, France, Russia, and the United States took Guangdong's provincial capital; Tingxiang memorialized asking to seal goods and close the ports, using favor and severity together; the emperor said grain transport by sea was underway, provocation would cause trouble, empty threats brought no real gain, and did not approve.
translations.idiomatic: When Anglo-French-Russian-American forces took Guangzhou, Tingxiang urged sealing trade and closing ports with a mix of conciliation and force; the emperor refused, fearing provocation would disrupt grain fleets at sea.

sentences.zh: 八年四月，英兵北犯，佔大沽砲台，窺內河。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the eighth year, British troops invaded north, seized the Dagu batteries, and probed the inner rivers.
translations.idiomatic: In April 1858 British troops moved north, seized the Dagu forts, and probed inland waterways.

sentences.zh: 大沽口外積沙，海舟不能直入，敵舟至，數以小汽船採測。

translations.literal: Outside Dagu mouth sand had accumulated so sea vessels could not enter directly; when enemy ships came they often used small steam launches to survey.
translations.idiomatic: Sand bars outside Dagu kept deep-draft ships out; enemy vessels sent small steam launches to sound the channels.

sentences.zh: 時方議款，不為備，不虞其驟發。

translations.literal: Peace talks were underway and no preparations were made; no one expected a sudden attack.
translations.idiomatic: Talks were underway and defenses were neglected; no one expected a sudden strike.

sentences.zh: 欽差大臣僧格林沁劾廷襄，奪官戍軍台。

translations.literal: Imperial commissioner Sengge Rinchen impeached Tingxiang, stripped his office, and sent him to garrison duty at the military colonies.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial commissioner Sengge Rinchen impeached Tingxiang, removed him from office, and exiled him to garrison duty.

sentences.zh: 九年，以三品頂戴署陝西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, with third-rank insignia he acted as governor of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1859 he returned as acting Shaanxi governor with third-rank insignia.

sentences.zh: 上命直省禁習天主教，廷襄疏言：「天主教流行中國二百餘年，到處窮搜，轉滋駭愕。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered provinces to forbid Catholic practice; Tingxiang memorialized: "Catholicism has spread in China over two hundred years; searching everywhere only increases alarm.
translations.idiomatic: When the court ordered provinces to suppress Catholicism, Tingxiang wrote: "It has been in China over two centuries; sweeping searches only spread panic.

sentences.zh: 惟有密飭官吏稽查保甲，列冊密記，乘機啟導。」

translations.literal: Only secretly order officials to inspect through baojia, list names in secret registers, and guide people when opportunity arises."
translations.idiomatic: He urged secret baojia inspections, covert registers, and gradual persuasion instead."

sentences.zh: 時款議未定，或請西巡，偕總督樂斌疏陳三便三難，議乃寢。

translations.literal: Peace terms were unsettled; some proposed moving the court west; together with Governor Le Bin he memorialized three advantages and three difficulties, and the plan was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: With treaties still unsettled, a western flight was proposed; Tingxiang and Governor Le Bin listed three pros and three cons, and the idea was dropped.

sentences.zh: 十一年，授山東巡撫。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was appointed governor of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In 1861 he was appointed governor of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 頻歲軍興，山東諸郡縣群盜蜂起，皖捻入境，勾結土匪，滋擾幾遍。

translations.literal: Years of warfare had made bandits swarm in Shandong's prefectures and counties; Anhui Nian entered the province, colluding with local bandits, and disturbances spread nearly everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Years of war had filled Shandong with bandits; Nian rebels from Anhui joined local gangs until unrest spread nearly everywhere.

sentences.zh: 僧格林沁大軍駐山東督剿，廷襄率兵出省協助，並督各郡縣團練防剿兼施，具詳僧格林沁傳。

translations.literal: Sengge Rinchen's main army garrisoned Shandong to direct suppression; Tingxiang led troops outside the province to assist and supervised militia defense and pursuit in each county—detailed in Sengge Rinchen's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Sengge Rinchen's army directed suppression from Shandong; Tingxiang led provincial troops to help and organized county militias—treated fully in Sengge Rinchen's biography.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，兼署河東河道總督。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he also acted as Hedong River director-general.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 he also acted as Hedong River director-general.

sentences.zh: 三年，入為刑部侍郎，調工部，又調戶部。

translations.literal: In the third year he entered the capital as vice minister of Punishments, was transferred to Works, then to Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864 he became vice minister of Punishments, then Works, then Revenue.

sentences.zh: 五年，湖北巡撫曾國荃疏劾總督官文貪庸驕蹇，並以公使錢餽四川考官胡家玉、張晉裕等，上命尚書綿森及廷襄往按，並詰家玉。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Hubei governor Zeng Guoquan memorialized impeaching governor-general Guan Wen as greedy, incompetent, arrogant, and obstinate, and also for using public funds to give gifts to Sichuan examination officials Hu Jiayu, Zhang Jinyu, and others; the emperor ordered Minister Miansen and Tingxiang to investigate and also question Jiayu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1866 Hubei governor Zeng Guoquan impeached governor-general Guan Wen for greed, incompetence, and arrogance and for bribing Sichuan examination officials; Minister Miansen and Tingxiang were sent to investigate.

sentences.zh: 家玉言自四川還京，道湖北，官文等餽贐，以道梗改水程，無州縣支應，乃受以充費。

translations.literal: Jiayu said returning from Sichuan to the capital he passed through Hubei; Guan Wen and others gave gifts; because the road was blocked he changed to the water route, with no prefectural support, and accepted them to cover expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Jiayu said that returning from Sichuan via Hubei he accepted gifts from Guan Wen because land routes were blocked and he had no official support on the water route.

sentences.zh: 廷襄等至湖北，疏言：「丁、漕、鹽、釐、關稅、捐輸，實用實支，並無浮濫。

translations.literal: When Tingxiang and others reached Hubei they memorialized: "Land tax, grain transport, salt, lijin, customs duties, and donations were spent as received with no waste.
translations.idiomatic: In Hubei, Tingxiang reported that land tax, grain transport, salt, lijin, customs, and donations were spent as collected without waste.

sentences.zh: 惟漢陽竹木捐零星不請獎敘者，凡因公動用，例不報銷之項，​​由此動支，官文餽家玉等是實。」

translations.literal: Only minor Hanyang bamboo-and-timber levies not submitted for rewards—for public use, items normally not reimbursable—were drawn from this; Guan Wen's gifts to Jiayu and others were true."
translations.idiomatic: Only small Hanyang timber levies not filed for rewards—routine unreimbursed public expenses—had funded Guan Wen's gifts to the examiners."

sentences.zh: 上為罷官文。

translations.literal: The emperor dismissed Guan Wen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dismissed Guan Wen.

sentences.zh: 即令廷襄署總督，家玉等並下吏議。

translations.literal: Tingxiang was immediately ordered to act as governor-general; Jiayu and others were also referred to judicial review.
translations.idiomatic: Tingxiang was made acting governor-general; the examiners were referred for discipline.

sentences.zh: 御史佛爾國春劾國荃，言國荃亦以竹木稅治公廨，嚴責廷襄蒙蔽。

translations.literal: Censor Fo'erguochun impeached Guoquan, saying Guoquan also used bamboo-and-timber tax for the yamen, and severely blamed Tingxiang for concealment.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Fo'erguochun impeached Guoquan for the same timber-tax practice and accused Tingxiang of a cover-up.

sentences.zh: 廷襄等復疏陳國荃上官未久，無以竹木稅治公廨事，因言：「湖北三次陷賊，百端草創，不循例案，諸廢具舉，隨事設施。

translations.literal: Tingxiang and others memorialized again that Guoquan had not long taken office and had not used timber tax for the yamen, adding: "Hubei fell to rebels three times; everything was started anew, precedents were not followed, abandoned practices were restored, and measures were improvised as needed.
translations.idiomatic: Tingxiang replied that Guoquan had not long been in office and denied the charge, noting Hubei's three occupations by rebels and improvised wartime administration.

sentences.zh: 今以動用官款，加以處分，亦足示警。

translations.literal: Now to punish use of official funds is warning enough.
translations.idiomatic: Punishing misuse of official funds was warning enough.

sentences.zh: 若更罪及所受之人，路遠給貲，親喪承賻，皆罣吏議。

translations.literal: If recipients are also punished, travel allowances, mourning gifts—all fall under censorial discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Punishing recipients too would criminalize travel allowances and condolence gifts.

sentences.zh: 王道本人情，瑣屑煩苛，似非政體。」

translations.literal: Kingship accords with human feeling; petty severity seems unfit for government."
translations.idiomatic: Government should follow human decency; petty severity ill suits it."

sentences.zh: 於是諸受餽者皆置不問。

translations.literal: Thereupon all gift recipients were left unpunished.
translations.idiomatic: All gift recipients were left unpunished.

sentences.zh: 六年，上用前事奪官文總督，是冬，國荃亦以病乞罷。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the emperor used the earlier case to remove Guan Wen as governor-general; that winter Guoquan also begged leave on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In 1867 Guan Wen was finally removed; that winter Guoquan resigned for illness.

sentences.zh: 廷襄還京，署吏部侍郎，遷左都御史。

translations.literal: Tingxiang returned to the capital, acted as vice minister of Personnel, and was promoted to left censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Beijing, he acted as vice minister of Personnel and became left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 再遷刑部尚書，兼署吏部。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to minister of Punishments and also acted as minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to minister of Punishments and also acted as minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 九年，卒，贈太子少保，諡端恪。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he died; he was posthumously given Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and named Duankai.
translations.idiomatic: In 1870 he died and was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the name Duankai.

sentences.zh: 馬新貽，字穀山，山東菏澤人。

translations.literal: Ma Xinyi, style name Gushan, was a native of Heze, Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xinyi, whose style was Gushan, came from Heze in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 道光二十七年進士，安徽即用知縣，除建平，署合肥，以勤明稱。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Daoguang he passed the jinshi examination, was assigned as magistrate in Anhui, was appointed to Jianping, acted at Hefei, and was known for diligence and clarity.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi in 1847, was assigned as Anhui magistrate, served at Jianping and Hefei, and was known for diligence.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，粵匪擾安徽，淮南北群盜並起，新貽常在兵間。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng, Cantonese rebels disturbed Anhui; north and south of the Huai bandits rose together; Xinyi was constantly in the army.
translations.idiomatic: In 1853, as Taiping forces ravaged Anhui and Huai bandits rose, Xinyi was constantly in the field.

sentences.zh: 五年，從攻廬州巢湖，新貽擊敗援賊，迭破賊盛家橋、三河鎮、柘皋諸賊屯，尋克廬州。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, joining the attack on Luzhou and Chaohu, Xinyi defeated relief rebels and in succession broke rebel camps at Shengjiaqiao, Sanhe Town, and Zhegao, then took Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1855, campaigning at Luzhou and Chaohu, he routed relief forces and took rebel camps at Shengjiaqiao, Sanhe, and Zhegao before capturing Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 積功累擢知府，賜花翎，補廬州。

translations.literal: For accumulated merit he was repeatedly promoted to prefect, given the peacock feather, and appointed to Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he rose to prefect, received the peacock feather, and was appointed to Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 七年，捻匪、粵匪合陷桃鎮，分擾上下派河，新貽破賊舒城，記名以道員用。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Nian and Cantonese rebels together took Taozhen and raided the upper and lower Pai Rivers; Xinyi defeated rebels at Shucheng and was registered for use as circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: In 1857, when Nian and Taiping forces took Taozhen, he beat them at Shucheng and was marked for circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 八年，署按察使。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he acted as provincial judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1858 he acted as provincial judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 賊犯廬州，新貽率練勇出城迎擊，賊間道入城，新貽軍潰失印，下吏議，革職留任。

translations.literal: Rebels attacked Luzhou; Xinyi led militia out to meet them; rebels entered the city by a side path; Xinyi's army collapsed and he lost his seal; judicial review followed, office stripped but retained in post.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels attacked Luzhou he led militia out; they entered by a side path, his force collapsed, he lost his seal, and was stripped of rank but kept on duty.

sentences.zh: 九年，丁母憂，巡撫翁同書奏請留署。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, on his mother's death, Governor Weng Tonghe memorialized asking him to remain in acting office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1859, mourning his mother, he was allowed to stay in acting office at Weng Tonghe's request.

sentences.zh: 十年，欽差大臣袁甲三為奏請復官。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Imperial Commissioner Yuan Jiasan memorialized asking restoration of his rank.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860 Imperial Commissioner Yuan Jiasan sought his reinstatement.

sentences.zh: 十一年，同書復奏薦，命以道員候補。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Tonghe again memorialized recommending him; he was ordered to await appointment as circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: In 1861 Weng Tonghe recommended him again and he was queued for circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，甲三復奏請留軍。

translations.literal: On his father's death, Jiasan again memorialized asking him to remain with the army.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, Yuan Jiasan asked that he remain with the army.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，從克廬州，敗賊壽州吳山廟，加按察使銜，署布政使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, joining the capture of Luzhou and defeating rebels at Wushan Temple in Shouzhou, he was given the rank of judicial commissioner and acted as provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 he helped retake Luzhou, defeated rebels at Wushan Temple, and was made acting provincial treasurer with judicial commissioner rank.

sentences.zh: 苗沛霖叛，從署巡撫唐訓方守蒙城，屢破賊。

translations.literal: When Miao Peilin rebelled, he followed acting Governor Tang Xunfang in defending Mengcheng and repeatedly defeated rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When Miao Peilin rebelled, he followed Tang Xunfang at Mengcheng and won repeated victories.

sentences.zh: 二年，授按察使，尋遷布政使。

translations.literal: In the second year he was appointed judicial commissioner and soon promoted to provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 he was made judicial commissioner and soon provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 三年，擢浙江巡撫。

translations.literal: In the third year he was promoted to governor of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864 he was promoted to governor of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 浙江新定，民困未蘇，新貽至，奏蠲逋賦。

translations.literal: Zhejiang had just been pacified and the people were not yet recovered; when Xinyi arrived he memorialized remitting tax arrears.
translations.idiomatic: Zhejiang had just been pacified; on arrival he remitted tax arrears.

sentences.zh: 四年，復奏減杭、嘉、湖、金、衢、嚴、處七府浮收錢漕，又請罷漕運諸無名之費，上從之，命勒石永禁。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he again memorialized reducing excess grain-transport surcharges in Hangzhou, Jiaxing, Huzhou, Jinhua, Quzhou, Yanzhou, and Chuzhou—the seven prefectures—and asked to abolish unnamed grain-transport fees; the emperor agreed and ordered them carved in stone as a permanent ban.
translations.idiomatic: In 1865 he cut excess surcharges in seven prefectures and abolished unnamed transport fees; the emperor agreed and had the ban carved in stone.

sentences.zh: 築海寧石塘、紹興東塘，濬三江口。

translations.literal: He built the stone seawall at Haining and the east embankment at Shaoxing, and dredged the Sanjiang estuary.
translations.idiomatic: He built Haining's stone seawall and Shaoxing's east embankment and dredged the Sanjiang estuary.

sentences.zh: 岐海為盜賊窟穴，遣兵捕治，擒其魁。

translations.literal: Qihai was a pirate lair; he sent troops to suppress them and captured the ringleader.
translations.idiomatic: He suppressed pirates in Qihai and captured their leader.

sentences.zh: 厚於待士，會城諸書院皆興復，士群至肄業，新貽皆視若子弟，優以資用獎勵之。

translations.literal: He treated scholars generously; all provincial academies were restored; scholars flocked to study; Xinyi treated them like sons and generously supported them with funds and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: He generously revived provincial academies, treated students like sons, and supported them with funds.

sentences.zh: 嚴州、紹興被水，蠲賑覈實，災不為害。

translations.literal: Yanzhou and Shaoxing suffered floods; he remitted taxes and verified relief so disaster did not become harm.
translations.idiomatic: Floods in Yanzhou and Shaoxing were met with remissions and verified relief.

sentences.zh: 台州民悍，輒群聚械鬥，新貽奏：「地方官憚吏議，瞻顧消弭。

translations.literal: Taizhou people were fierce and often gathered for armed fights; Xinyi memorialized: "Local officials fear censorial discipline and hesitate to suppress incidents.
translations.idiomatic: Taizhou was prone to armed brawls; Xinyi wrote that officials feared discipline and let incidents fester.

sentences.zh: 請嗣後有諱匿不報者參處；

translations.literal: He asked that hereafter those who concealed and failed to report be punished;
translations.idiomatic: He asked that officials who concealed incidents be punished;

sentences.zh: 僅止失察，皆寬貸，仍責令捕治。」

translations.literal: if only negligent in oversight, all were leniently treated, but still ordered to capture and punish."
translations.idiomatic: mere negligence would be forgiven, but capture and punishment would still be required."

sentences.zh: 下部議行。

translations.literal: The ministries deliberated and implemented.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries adopted it.

sentences.zh: 象山、寧海有禁界地曰南田，方數百里，環海土寇邱財青等處窟其中，遣兵捕得財青置之法，南田乃安。

translations.literal: Xiangshan and Ninghai had forbidden border land called Nantian, several hundred li square; coastal bandits such as Qiu Caiqing lurked there; troops were sent, Caiqing was captured and executed by law, and Nantian was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He cleared Nantian—a forbidden coastal zone in Xiangshan and Ninghai—by capturing and executing bandit Qiu Caiqing.

sentences.zh: 黃岩總兵剛安泰出海捕盜，為所戕，檄副將張其光等擊殺盜五十餘。

translations.literal: Huangyan brigade general Gang Antai went to sea against pirates and was killed; Deputy Commander Zhang Qiguang and others were ordered to kill over fifty pirates.
translations.idiomatic: When brigade general Gang Antai was killed at sea, Zhang Qiguang destroyed over fifty pirates.

sentences.zh: 上以新貽未能豫防，下吏議。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Xinyi had not prevented it, referred him to judicial review.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor censured him for failing to prevent Gang's death.

sentences.zh: 嘉興、湖州北與蘇州界，皆水鄉，方亂時，民自衛置槍於船，謂之「槍船」，久之聚博行劫為民害。

translations.literal: Jiaxing and Huzhou north of the border with Suzhou are all water country; during the turmoil people put guns on boats for self-defense, called "gun boats"; in time they gathered to gamble and rob, harming the people.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiaxing-Huzhou waterways, wartime "gun boats" for self-defense had turned to gambling and robbery.

sentences.zh: 新貽會江蘇巡撫郭柏廕督兵擒斬其渠，及悍黨數十，槍船害始除。

translations.literal: Xinyi joined Jiangsu governor Guo Baiyin in directing troops to capture and behead the leaders and several tens of fierce followers; the gun-boat scourge was finally removed.
translations.idiomatic: With Jiangsu governor Guo Baiyin he destroyed gun-boat leaders and ended the scourge.

sentences.zh: 擢閩浙總督。

translations.literal: He was promoted to governor-general of Fujian-Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to governor-general of Fujian-Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 七年，調兩江總督，兼通商大臣。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to governor-general of the two Jiang provinces and also served as trade superintendent.
translations.idiomatic: In 1868 he became governor-general of Liang-Jiang and trade superintendent.

sentences.zh: 奏言：「標兵虛弱，無以壯根本。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "The banner troops are weak and cannot strengthen the foundation.
translations.idiomatic: He reported that banner garrisons were too weak to secure the region.

sentences.zh: 請選各營兵二千五百人屯江寧，親加訓練。」

translations.literal: He asked to select 2,500 men from each camp to garrison Jiangning and personally train them."
translations.idiomatic: He asked to train 2,500 selected men from each camp at Jiangning under his personal direction."

sentences.zh: 編為五營，令總兵劉啟發督率緝捕，盜為衰止。

translations.literal: They were organized into five battalions; Brigade General Liu Qifa was ordered to lead pursuit and capture; banditry declined.
translations.idiomatic: They formed five battalions under Liu Qifa; banditry declined.

sentences.zh: 宿遷設水、旱兩關，淮關於蔣壩設分關，並為商民擾累。

translations.literal: Suqian had water and land toll stations; the Huai customs set a branch at Jiangba—all burdensome to merchants and people.
translations.idiomatic: Suqian's twin toll stations and Huai customs' Jiangba branch burdened merchants.

sentences.zh: 新貽奏：「蔣壩為安徽鳳陽關轄境，淮關遠隔洪澤湖，不應設為子口。

translations.literal: Xinyi memorialized: "Jiangba is within Anhui's Fengyang customs jurisdiction; Huai customs is far across Hongze Lake and should not have a sub-station.
translations.idiomatic: He argued Jiangba belonged to Fengyang customs and Huai customs should not operate a distant sub-station.

sentences.zh: 當令淮關監督申明舊例，嚴禁需索。

translations.literal: The Huai customs superintendent should clarify old rules and strictly forbid exactions.
translations.idiomatic: Huai customs should enforce old rules and forbid exactions.

sentences.zh: 宿遷旱關非舊例，徵數微，請裁撤，專收水關。」

translations.literal: Suqian's land toll was not old precedent and collected little; he asked to abolish it and collect only at the water station."
translations.idiomatic: He asked to abolish Suqian's minor land toll and keep only the water station."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 幅匪高歸等在山東、江蘇交界佔民圩，行劫，新貽捕誅其渠。

translations.literal: Bandit Gao Gui and others on the Shandong-Jiangsu border occupied people's embankments and robbed; Xinyi captured and executed the leaders.
translations.idiomatic: He executed bandit leader Gao Gui, who had raided the Shandong-Jiangsu border.

sentences.zh: 九年七月，新貽赴署西偏箭道閱射，事畢步還署。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the ninth year, Xinyi went to the western archery range of the yamen to review shooting; when finished he walked back to the yamen.
translations.idiomatic: In July 1870 he reviewed archery at the yamen's western range and walked back afterward.

sentences.zh: 甫及門，有張汶祥者突出，偽若陳狀，抽刀擊新貽，傷脅，次日卒。

translations.literal: Just at the gate, Zhang Wenxiang suddenly rushed out, feigning to present a petition, drew a knife and struck Xinyi, wounding his ribs; he died the next day.
translations.idiomatic: At the gate Zhang Wenxiang feigned a petition, stabbed him in the ribs, and he died the next day.

sentences.zh: 將軍魁玉以聞，上震悼，賜卹，贈太子太保，予騎都尉兼雲騎尉世職，諡端愍。

translations.literal: General Kuiyu reported it; the emperor was deeply grieved, granted condolence funds, posthumously made him Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, gave hereditary ranks of Cavalry Commandant and Cloud Cavalry Captain, and named him Duanyin.
translations.idiomatic: General Kuiyu reported the murder; the emperor mourned, enriched his family, made him Grand Guardian posthumously, granted hereditary ranks, and named him Duanyin.

sentences.zh: 命魁玉署總督，嚴鞫汶祥，詞反覆屢變。

translations.literal: Kuiyu was ordered to act as governor-general and strictly interrogate Wenxiang, whose statements repeatedly changed.
translations.idiomatic: Kuiyu acted as governor-general and interrogated Wenxiang, whose story kept changing.

sentences.zh: 給事中王書瑞奏請根究主使，命漕運總督張之萬會訊。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Wang Shurui memorialized asking to trace the mastermind; Grain Transport Director-General Zhang Zhiwan was ordered to join the inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shurui demanded the mastermind; Zhang Zhiwan joined the investigation.

sentences.zh: 之萬等以獄辭上，略言：「汶祥嘗從粵匪，复通海盜。

translations.literal: Zhiwan and others submitted the case, saying in summary: "Wenxiang once followed Cantonese rebels and later joined sea pirates.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhiwan reported that Wenxiang had served Taiping forces and later pirates.

sentences.zh: 新貽撫浙江，捕殺南田海盜，其黨多被戮，妻為人所略。

translations.literal: When Xinyi governed Zhejiang he captured and killed Nantian pirates; many of their party were executed; his wife was abducted.
translations.idiomatic: As Zhejiang governor Xinyi had crushed Nantian pirates, killing many; Wenxiang's wife was abducted.

sentences.zh: 新貽閱兵至寧波，呈訴不准，以是挾仇，無他人指使。

translations.literal: When Xinyi reviewed troops at Ningbo, Wenxiang presented a grievance that was not accepted; he bore a grudge; no one else directed him.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang's petition at Ningbo was rejected; he acted from private revenge, not on orders.

sentences.zh: 請以大逆定罪。」

translations.literal: He asked conviction for great treason."
translations.idiomatic: He sought conviction for treason."

sentences.zh: 復命刑部尚書鄭敦謹馳往，會總督曾國籓覆訊，仍如原讞，汶祥極刑，並戮其子，上從之。

translations.literal: The Minister of Punishments Zheng Dunjin was again ordered to hurry there; joining Governor-General Zeng Guofan for re-examination, the original verdict stood; Wenxiang suffered extreme punishment and his son was also executed; the emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Zheng Dunjin and Zeng Guofan confirmed the verdict; Wenxiang and his son were executed.

sentences.zh: 新貽官安徽、浙江皆得民心，治兩江繼曾國籓後，長於綜覈，鎮定不擾。

translations.literal: Xinyi as official in Anhui and Zhejiang won popular hearts; governing Liang-Jiang after Zeng Guofan he excelled at comprehensive review, calm and unperturbing.
translations.idiomatic: He won hearts in Anhui and Zhejiang; succeeding Zeng Guofan at Liang-Jiang he was thorough, calm, and steady.

sentences.zh: 江寧、安慶、杭州、海塘並建專祠。

translations.literal: Dedicated shrines were built at Jiangning, Anqing, Hangzhou, and the seawall.
translations.idiomatic: Shrines were raised at Jiangning, Anqing, Hangzhou, and the seawall.

sentences.zh: 李宗羲，字雨亭，四川開縣人。

translations.literal: Li Zongxi, style name Yuting, was a native of Kaixian, Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zongxi, whose style was Yuting, came from Kaixian in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 道光二十七年進士，安徽即用知縣，歷英山、婺源、太平。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Daoguang he passed the jinshi examination, was assigned as magistrate in Anhui, and served Yingshan, Wuyuan, and Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi in 1847, was assigned to Anhui, and served at Yingshan, Wuyuan, and Taiping.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，粵匪陷安慶，宗羲奉檄詣廬州軍督糧械，積功累擢知府。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng, Cantonese rebels took Anqing; Zongxi received orders to go to the Luzhou army to supervise grain and weapons, and for accumulated merit was repeatedly promoted to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In 1853, when Anqing fell, he supplied the Luzhou army and rose to prefect for merit.

sentences.zh: 八年，曾國籓進規安徽，調充營務處。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, when Zeng Guofan advanced into Anhui, he was transferred to the camp affairs office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1858 he joined Zeng Guofan's Anhui campaign staff.

sentences.zh: 九年，署安慶知府，以疾去官。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he acted as prefect of Anqing and left office because of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In 1859 he acted as Anqing prefect but resigned for illness.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，河南巡撫嚴樹森疏薦，命送部引見，樹森旋撫湖北，又疏調從軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, Henan Governor Yan Shusen memorialized recommending him; he was ordered to the ministry for audience; Shusen soon governed Hubei and again memorialized transferring him to the army.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 Yan Shusen recommended him; after audience he joined Shusen's Hubei staff.

sentences.zh: 三年，曾國籓督兩江，調赴兩江筦江北釐金總局，裁定沿江釐捐科則。

translations.literal: In the third year, when Zeng Guofan governed Liang-Jiang, he was transferred to manage the North-of-the-River lijin general bureau and fix lijin rates along the river.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864 Zeng Guofan put him in charge of north-of-the-Yangtze lijin and fixed river rates.

sentences.zh: 江寧克復，以道員歸兩江補用。

translations.literal: When Jiangning was recovered, he returned to Liang-Jiang for appointment as circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiangning's recovery he was appointed circuit intendant in Liang-Jiang.

sentences.zh: 四年，署兩淮鹽運使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he acted as Liang-Huai salt transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1865 he acted as Liang-Huai salt commissioner.

sentences.zh: 自軍興，淮南鹽艘改道泰興，宗羲於瓜洲東別濬新河，避長江風濤之險，商​​民便之。

translations.literal: Since warfare began, Huainan salt barges had been rerouted through Taixing; Zongxi dredged a new canal east of Guazhou to avoid Yangtze storms; merchants and people found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: He opened a new canal east of Guazhou so Huainan salt could avoid Yangtze storms after the war rerouted traffic through Taixing.

sentences.zh: 遷安徽按察使，再遷江寧布政使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Anhui judicial commissioner and again to Jiangning provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: He became Anhui judicial commissioner, then Jiangning provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 五年，清水潭決，被災者七州縣，宗羲工賑並行，活民甚眾。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Qingshui Tan breached; seven prefectures and counties were affected; Zongxi carried out relief and public works together and saved very many people.
translations.idiomatic: In 1866, when Qingshui Tan burst its banks and seven prefectures and counties were flooded, Zongxi combined relief work with engineering and saved a great many lives.

sentences.zh: 定招墾荒田酌緩昇科限制章程，及江寧七屬民衛丁漕折徵等次，民皆稱便。

translations.literal: He fixed regulations for recruiting reclamation of wasteland with graduated tax relief, and grades for converting grain tribute and land tax among the seven Jiangning subprefectures for civilian and garrison households; the people all praised the convenience.
translations.idiomatic: He set rules for reclaiming wasteland with phased tax relief and standardized grain-tribute and land-tax conversion for Jiangning’s seven subordinate districts, to general public approval.

sentences.zh: 八年，擢山西巡撫，劾布政使胡大任廢弛因循，罷之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was promoted to Governor of Shanxi, impeached Provincial Treasurer Hu Daren for laxity and procrastination, and dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: In 1869 he became Shanxi governor, impeached the provincial treasurer Hu Daren for negligence, and had him removed.

sentences.zh: 令按察使李慶★等率兵分地駐防，陝回乘河冰來犯，三戰皆捷；

translations.literal: He ordered Judicial Commissioner Li Qingtang and others to lead troops to garrison by district; Shaanxi Muslims took advantage of river ice to attack, and in three battles all were victorious;
translations.idiomatic: He posted Judicial Commissioner Li Qingtang and others to garrison the province by district; when Shaanxi Muslim rebels crossed the frozen river, he won three successive battles;

sentences.zh: 屢自延川、韓城東竄，並擊走之。

translations.literal: They repeatedly fled east from Yanchuan and Hancheng, and he drove them off each time.
translations.idiomatic: and repeatedly drove off raids eastward from Yanchuan and Hancheng.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂去官。

translations.literal: He left office upon entering mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 十二年，服闋，擢兩江總督。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, when mourning ended, he was promoted to Governor-General of Liang-Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1873, after mourning, he was appointed governor-general of Liang-Jiang.

sentences.zh: 日本方構釁，宗羲治江防，增築沿江烏龍山、江陰都天廟、象山、焦山、下關砲台。

translations.literal: Japan was then provoking trouble; Zongxi managed river defense and added fortifications along the river at Wulong Shan, Jiangyin Dutian Temple, Xiang Shan, Jiao Shan, and Xiaoguan.
translations.idiomatic: With Japan stirring trouble, he strengthened river defenses, adding batteries at Wulong Shan, Jiangyin’s Dutian Temple, Xiang Shan, Jiao Shan, and Xiaoguan.

sentences.zh: 又於吳淞口及江陰北岸瀏聞沙、烏龍山北岸沙洲圩次第添築，使江、海相犄角。

translations.literal: He also added works in succession at Wusong mouth and on the north bank of Jiangyin at Liulian Sha and the sand-bank polder on the north bank of Wulong Shan, so that the river and sea formed mutual horns.
translations.idiomatic: He also built up Liulian Sha and the Wulong Shan north-bank sand polder at Wusong and north Jiangyin so river and sea defenses supported each other.

sentences.zh: 時詔修圓明園，宗羲疏言：「外侮內患，天時人事，皆有可慮。

translations.literal: At that time an edict ordered repairs to the Yuanmingyuan; Zongxi memorialized, saying: "Foreign aggression and internal troubles, the signs of heaven and affairs of men, all give cause for concern.
translations.idiomatic: When the court ordered repairs to the Yuanmingyuan, Zongxi memorialized: “Foreign threats and domestic troubles—heaven’s signs and human affairs alike give cause for alarm.

sentences.zh: 請省營繕，減服禦。」

translations.literal: I ask that construction be reduced and court dress and rites simplified."
translations.idiomatic: Cut building projects and reduce court expenditure and ceremonial display.”

sentences.zh: 十三年，又疏言：「星變屢見，外患方熾。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he again memorialized, saying: "Unusual stars have repeatedly appeared, and foreign troubles are blazing.
translations.idiomatic: In 1874 he memorialized again: “Heavenly portents have recurred and foreign aggression is intensifying.

sentences.zh: 上年御史沈淮奏請停止園工，臣亦冒貢愚忱。

translations.literal: Last year Censor Shen Huai memorialized asking that work on the gardens be stopped, and I too ventured my sincere counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Last year Censor Shen Huai asked that garden work be halted, and I too offered my counsel.

sentences.zh: 茲復有不能已於言者，時局艱難，度支短絀，特一端耳。

translations.literal: Now there is more that I cannot refrain from saying: the times are hard, and revenue is short—that is only one aspect.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I must speak again: hard times and empty coffers are only part of the problem.

sentences.zh: 今外人入處肘腋，圓明園距京城數十里，既無堅城管鑰之固，复少大枝護衛之兵。

translations.literal: Now foreigners are within arm’s reach of the armpit; the Yuanmingyuan is several tens of li from the capital, with neither the firmness of strong walls and guarded gates, nor many large branches of protecting troops.
translations.idiomatic: Foreigners now stand at the capital’s very threshold. The Yuanmingyuan lies only a few dozen li from Beijing, without strong walls or a large guard force.

sentences.zh: 頻年以來，每遇民、教爭鬥，外人動挾兵船要求。

translations.literal: In recent years, whenever there were clashes between people and missionaries, foreigners invariably brought gunboats to make demands.
translations.idiomatic: In recent clashes between locals and missionaries, foreigners have repeatedly sent gunboats to press demands.

sentences.zh: 天津朝警，則海淀夕驚。

translations.literal: When Tianjin was alarmed in the morning, Haidian was alarmed in the evening.
translations.idiomatic: Alarm at Tianjin in the morning meant alarm at Haidian by evening.

sentences.zh: 皇上奉皇太后於此，此臣所萬分不安者也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty accompanies the Empress Dowager there—this is what fills your servant with utmost unease.
translations.idiomatic: That Your Majesty and the Empress Dowager stay there fills me with the deepest unease.

sentences.zh: 如蒙皇上乾綱立斷，速諭停工，天下臣民，知皇上有臥薪嘗膽之思，必共振敵愾同仇之氣。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty, with decisive imperial authority, swiftly orders work halted, the officials and people under heaven, knowing that the Emperor harbors thoughts of sleeping on brushwood and tasting gall, will surely together rouse the spirit of shared hatred of the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty decisively halts the work, the people will see resolve to endure hardship and avenge humiliation, and will rally against the enemy.

sentences.zh: 人主居崇高之位，持威福之柄，苟無敬畏之念，則驕肆之心生；

translations.literal: A ruler occupying a lofty position and holding the handle of authority and favor—if he lacks a mind of reverence, a heart of arrogance and license arises;
translations.idiomatic: A ruler on a lofty throne, wielding power without reverence, grows arrogant;

sentences.zh: 苟無忠諤之臣，則讒諂之人至。

translations.literal: if he lacks loyal and outspoken ministers, then sycophants arrive.
translations.idiomatic: without loyal critics, flatterers gain access.

sentences.zh: 近日大學士文祥引疾，侍郎桂清外調，道路頗有惜詞。

translations.literal: Recently Grand Secretary Wenxiang cited illness to withdraw, and Vice Minister Gui Qing was transferred elsewhere; along the roads there were many expressions of regret.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Wenxiang has lately retired on grounds of illness and Vice Minister Gui Qing has been transferred—people along the roads speak with regret.

sentences.zh: 臣竊謂老成憂國者，宜留之左右，以輔成聖德；

translations.literal: Your servant ventures to think that those of mature years who worry for the state should be kept at the ruler’s side to help complete sagely virtue;
translations.idiomatic: Veteran statesmen who care for the realm should be kept close to help form imperial virtue;

sentences.zh: 忠直敢諫者，宜誘之使言，以恢張聖聽。」

translations.literal: those loyal, upright, and daring in remonstrance should be encouraged to speak, to broaden the sage’s hearing."
translations.idiomatic: and forthright remonstrators should be encouraged to speak and widen the Emperor’s hearing.

sentences.zh: 疏入，上嘉納之。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the Emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised and accepted the memorial.

sentences.zh: 總理各國事務衙門籌議海防六事，下各督撫詳議，宗羲上疏曰：「萬事根本，以用人為要，而就海防言，尤以求將才為要。

translations.literal: The Zongli Yamen deliberated six matters for coastal defense and sent them down to each governor and governor-general for detailed discussion; Zongxi memorialized, saying: "Of all things the root is employing men, and speaking of coastal defense, seeking general talent is especially the root.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zongli Yamen drafted six coastal-defense proposals for governors to discuss, Zongxi wrote: “Everything rests on appointing the right men; for coastal defense, finding capable commanders matters most.

sentences.zh: 宋臣楊萬里有言：'相不厭舊，將不厭新。

translations.literal: A Song official, Yang Wanli, had a saying: 'Ministers do not dislike the old; generals do not dislike the new.
translations.idiomatic: As the Song official Yang Wanli said, ‘Do not cling to old ministers; seek new generals.’

sentences.zh: '蓋言用兵忌暮氣，宜年壯氣銳，素有遠志，未建大功之人。

translations.literal: This is to say that in using troops one must beware of the spirit of old age; one should choose men young in years and sharp in spirit, who have long harbored far-reaching ambition and have not yet achieved great merit.
translations.idiomatic: War demands vigor, not stale habit—men still young, ambitious, and not yet bloated with past honors.

sentences.zh: 至宿將勳臣，帝心簡在，固無俟臣下之論列也。

translations.literal: As for veteran generals and meritorious ministers, the Emperor’s mind already rests upon them; there is indeed no need for discussion by those below.
translations.idiomatic: Veteran commanders already enjoy the Emperor’s trust and need no recommendation from me.

sentences.zh: 古有海防無海戰，今練兵仍以水陸兼練為主。

translations.literal: In antiquity there was coastal defense but no naval battle; today in drilling troops one should still take combined land-and-sea training as primary.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient coastal defense did not mean naval battle, but training should still combine land and sea forces.

sentences.zh: 水師戰艦不及輪船，輪船又不及鐵甲，而船之得力與否，仍視乎駕馭之人。

translations.literal: War junks cannot match steamships, and steamships cannot match ironclads; yet whether a ship proves effective still depends on those who command it.
translations.idiomatic: War junks fall short of steamers, steamers of ironclads—but ships are only as good as the men who sail them.

sentences.zh: 今戰艦即不能一時盡易，應就弁兵中挑赴輪船學習，仍歸水師提督節制。
