translations.literal: Since war junks cannot all be replaced at once, officers and soldiers should be selected from among them to study aboard steamships, still under the control of the naval commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Until the fleet can be replaced, select officers and men for steamer training under the naval commander.

sentences.zh: 更招集沿海熟習沙線，能耐勞苦之人，參用西法，加以訓練。

translations.literal: Recruit moreover coastal people skilled in sandbars and able to endure hardship, apply Western methods, and give them training.
translations.idiomatic: Recruit coastal men who know the shoals and can endure hardship, train them in Western methods.

sentences.zh: 然沿海地廣，勢不能遍設輪船，若敵乘無備，舍舟登陸，則我船砲皆無所用，故不可不急練陸兵。

translations.literal: Yet the coast is broad and it is impossible to station steamships everywhere; if the enemy, finding us unprepared, abandons boats and lands, then our ships and guns are all useless—therefore land troops must urgently be drilled.
translations.idiomatic: The coast is too long to cover entirely with steamers; if the enemy lands where we are weak, ships and guns avail nothing—land forces must be drilled urgently.

sentences.zh: 同治十年，曾國籓議沿海奉天、直隸、山東、江蘇、浙江、福建、廣東七省練陸兵九萬，沿江安徽、江西、湖北三省練陸兵三萬，合成十二萬。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Tongzhi, Zeng Guofan proposed drilling ninety thousand land troops in the seven coastal provinces of Fengtian, Zhili, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, and Guangdong, and thirty thousand land troops in the three Yangtze provinces of Anhui, Jiangxi, and Hubei, totaling one hundred twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In 1871 Zeng Guofan proposed 90,000 coastal troops in seven provinces and 30,000 in three Yangtze provinces—120,000 in all.

sentences.zh: 以陸兵為御敵之資，以輪船為調兵之用，海道雖極遼遠，血脈皆可貫通。

translations.literal: Take land troops as the resource for resisting the enemy, and steamships as the means for moving troops; though sea routes are extremely distant, the arteries can all be connected.
translations.idiomatic: Land forces should hold the line; steamers should move them—so distant coasts remain linked.

sentences.zh: 今誠踵其議而力行之，各省分定數目，各專責成，貴精不貴多，宜聚不宜散。

translations.literal: If now we truly follow that proposal and earnestly carry it out, each province fixing its quota and each bearing sole responsibility, valuing quality not quantity, gathering not dispersing—
translations.idiomatic: Follow that plan in earnest: fix quotas by province, demand results, favor quality over numbers, and keep forces concentrated.

sentences.zh: 從前缺額之兵，不必再補，現在已募之勇，更加精練，是在平時之實力講求矣。

translations.literal: the vacancies of former years need not be filled again; the braves already recruited should be further refined in drill—the matter lies in earnest pursuit of real strength in peacetime.
translations.idiomatic: Do not refill old vacancies; drill the men already raised. Real strength is built in peace.

sentences.zh: 西洋火器，日新月異，疊出不窮。

translations.literal: Western firearms change day by day, new models appearing without end.
translations.idiomatic: Western firearms improve constantly, with new models appearing endlessly.

sentences.zh: 今日所謂巧，即後日所謂拙。

translations.literal: What is called clever today is what will be called clumsy tomorrow.
translations.idiomatic: Today’s marvel is tomorrow’s obsolete weapon.

sentences.zh: 論中國自強之策，決非專恃火器所能制勝。

translations.literal: Speaking of China’s policy for strengthening itself, victory cannot depend solely on firearms.
translations.idiomatic: China cannot win by relying on firearms alone.

sentences.zh: 然風會所趨，有不能不相隨轉移者。

translations.literal: Yet the trend of the times has aspects that cannot but shift together with it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the times compel us to adapt whether we wish it or not.

sentences.zh: 各國新出之砲，現在上海機器局已能如式製造。

translations.literal: The newest guns of the various countries can already be manufactured to pattern at the Shanghai machine works.
translations.idiomatic: Shanghai’s arsenals can already copy the latest foreign cannon.

sentences.zh: 惟火器不難於用而難於不用。

translations.literal: Only with firearms, the difficulty lies not in using them but in not using them.
translations.idiomatic: The problem with firearms is not using them but neglecting them.

sentences.zh: 有事試演，尚可經久，無事擱置，立形銹壞。

translations.literal: When there is business they are tested in drill and can last long; when there is no business and they are set aside, they quickly rust and break.
translations.idiomatic: Drilled in use they last; left idle they rust at once.

sentences.zh: 以後購造槍砲，應於操演之後，時時磨洗，不許銹壞，違者罪之，是珍惜巨帑之要義。

translations.literal: Henceforth in purchasing and making guns and cannon, after drill they should constantly be cleaned and not allowed to rust; violators should be punished—this is the essential meaning of cherishing great funds.
translations.idiomatic: After purchase and drill, guns and cannon must be cleaned and maintained on pain of punishment—that is how to safeguard public funds.

sentences.zh: 臣聞自古覘國勢者，在人材之盛衰，不在財用之贏絀；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that since antiquity those who observe a state’s power look to the rise and fall of talent, not to surplus or shortage of revenue;
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity, observers have judged a state’s strength by its talent, not its treasury;

sentences.zh: 在政事之得失，不在兵力之強弱：未聞以器械為重輕也。

translations.literal: to the gain and loss of governance, not to the strength or weakness of military force: one has never heard of taking weapons as the weight of importance.
translations.idiomatic: by the quality of government, not the size of armies—never by arsenals alone.

sentences.zh: 且西人之所以強者，其心志和而齊，其法制簡而嚴，其取人必課實用，其任事者無欺誑侵漁之習，其選兵甚精，故臨陣勇敢而不畏死。

translations.literal: Moreover, the reason Westerners are strong is that their minds are harmonious and united, their laws simple and strict, their selection of men always tests practical ability, those who handle affairs have no habit of deception and embezzlement, and their choice of soldiers is very careful—therefore in battle they are brave and do not fear death.
translations.idiomatic: Western strength rests on unity of purpose, simple strict law, merit-based appointment, honest administration, and careful selection of soldiers who fight without fear.

sentences.zh: 不察其所以強，而徒效其器械，豈足恃哉？

translations.literal: If one does not examine the reason they are strong but merely imitates their weapons, how can that be relied upon?
translations.idiomatic: Copy their weapons without understanding why they are strong, and we gain little.

sentences.zh: 自福建創設機器局，上海繼之，江寧、天津又繼之，皆由槍砲而推及輪船。

translations.literal: Since machine works were established in Fujian, Shanghai followed, and Jiangning and Tianjin followed again—all proceeding from guns and cannon to extend to steamships.
translations.idiomatic: Arsenals spread from Fujian to Shanghai, Jiangning, and Tianjin, moving from guns to steamships.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為大沽、吳淞、直、東、閩、廣等口，如能各得鐵甲一二，蚊子船三四，佐以兵輪，安配重大擊遠之砲，與砲台相輔，亦足屹成重鎮，稍戢戎心。

translations.literal: Your servant thinks that if Dagu, Wusong, Zhili, Shandong, Fujian, Guangdong, and other ports could each obtain one or two ironclads and three or four gunboats, assisted by armed steamers fitted with heavy long-range cannon to support the batteries, that would suffice to stand as strong points and somewhat restrain the enemy’s heart.
translations.idiomatic: Give each major port one or two ironclads and several gunboats, backed by armed steamers with heavy guns, and batteries would form a credible defense and curb enemy ambitions.

sentences.zh: 惟泰西各國輪船以百數十計，鐵甲船以數十計，​​大砲以千計，小砲以數千計，即使中國歲籌巨款，多方製造，亦必不能如彼之多且精也。

translations.literal: Only the steamships of Western countries number in the hundreds and tens, ironclads in the tens, large cannon in the thousands, and small cannon in the thousands; even if China every year raised huge funds and manufactured on many sides, it still could not match their quantity and quality.
translations.idiomatic: Western powers field scores of ironclads, hundreds of steamers, and thousands of guns; China cannot match their scale even with vast annual spending.

sentences.zh: 臣謂船砲當量力徐圖，而仍以修政事、造人材為本，使各國鄉風慕義，或外侮可以稍紓。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that ships and cannon should be pursued according to capacity and by gradual steps, while still taking improving governance and creating talent as the root, so that the customs of the various countries may admire righteousness, and foreign aggression may be somewhat eased.
translations.idiomatic: Build ships and guns as means allow, but make good government and cultivating talent the foundation—then foreign pressure may ease.

sentences.zh: 近年勸捐、收釐、津貼，無法不備，民力竭矣。

translations.literal: In recent years in soliciting donations, collecting lijin, and imposing surcharges, no method has been left unused; the people’s strength is exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Donations, lijin, and surcharges have exhausted the people.

sentences.zh: 煤、鐵乃中國自然之利，若一一開採，不獨造船造砲取之裕如，且可以致富強。

translations.literal: Coal and iron are China’s natural advantages; if each is opened and mined, not only will building ships and making cannon draw on them abundantly, but wealth and strength can also be attained.
translations.idiomatic: Coal and iron are native resources; develop them and shipbuilding and armaments will prosper—and with them national strength.

sentences.zh: 現在磁州業已奏明試辦，而湖南、福建、江西、山西等省已成之煤、鐵廠，擴而行之，果能有效，何必捨近求遠，取給外國？

translations.literal: At present trial operations at Cizhou have already been memorialized and approved, while coal and iron works already established in Hunan, Fujian, Jiangxi, Shanxi, and other provinces, if expanded and carried out, should they prove effective—why abandon what is near and seek what is far, drawing supply from foreign countries?
translations.idiomatic: Cizhou is already in trial; expand existing mines in Hunan, Fujian, Jiangxi, and Shanxi rather than buy abroad when domestic supply suffices.

sentences.zh: 為目前權宜計，將各口洋稅通提六成，專供海防之用，五年為限，當可集事。

translations.literal: As a temporary expedient for the present, let sixty percent of customs duties at each port be drawn in total and devoted solely to coastal defense, with a limit of five years—then the task can be accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: For now, allocate sixty percent of port customs revenue to coastal defense for five years—that should fund the effort.

sentences.zh: 若夫節流之法，更非難行。

translations.literal: As for methods of cutting expenditure, they are even less difficult to carry out.
translations.idiomatic: Cutting expenditure is easier still.

sentences.zh: 節之必自朝廷始，誠能罷土木之工，省傳辦之費，減宮中之用，則一歲所省，何啻百萬？

translations.literal: Cutting must begin with the court itself; if construction projects can truly be stopped, costs for special imperial orders reduced, and palace expenses lessened, then in one year what is saved—how is it less than a million?
translations.idiomatic: Begin at court: halt construction, cut special orders, reduce palace spending—and a million taels may be saved in a year.

sentences.zh: 各省督撫，盡裁不急之費，錢漕稅釐，實力稽察，勿使乾沒，則一歲所增，何啻百萬？

translations.literal: If each provincial governor and governor-general entirely cut non-urgent expenses, and grain transport, land tax, and lijin were earnestly audited so that nothing was embezzled, then in one year what is gained—how is it less than a million?
translations.idiomatic: Governors should cut waste and audit grain, land tax, and lijin so nothing is stolen—another million may be gained.

sentences.zh: 請敕下戶部，統籌全局，分別出入，於綜覈各項之外，指定籌防專款，應用若干，俾中外上下曉然於經費之有限，財用之有制，力求撙節，不必言利，而度支可裕矣。

translations.literal: I ask that the Ministry of Revenue be ordered to plan the whole situation, distinguish receipts and disbursements, and beyond consolidating all items designate a special fund for defense, stating how much should be applied, so that court and provinces, high and low, clearly understand that funds are limited and expenditure has rules, striving for thrift without needing to speak of profit—and then revenue can be ample.
translations.idiomatic: Let the Board of Revenue plan overall finances, set aside a dedicated defense fund, and make limits clear at every level—thrift, not profiteering, will balance the books.

sentences.zh: 以上皆就原奏四事推廣言之，要必得人而後可以言持久。

translations.literal: The above all expand upon the four matters of the original memorial; the essential is that only after obtaining the right men can one speak of lasting success.
translations.idiomatic: These points extend the original four proposals—but lasting success depends first on the right men.

sentences.zh: 臣週諮博採，事之可行者，尚有三端。

translations.literal: Your servant, consulting widely and gathering information, finds that among feasible measures there are still three further points.
translations.idiomatic: After wide consultation, I see three further measures worth trying.

sentences.zh: 沿海各島，大都土瘠產薄，惟台灣形勢雄勝，與廈門相犄角。

translations.literal: Coastal islands are mostly poor in soil and thin in produce; only Taiwan’s terrain is powerfully advantageous and forms horns with Xiamen.
translations.idiomatic: Most coastal islands are barren; only Taiwan’s position is commanding and pairs with Xiamen.

sentences.zh: 東南俯瞰噶囉巴、呂宋，西南遙制越南、暹羅、緬甸、新加坡，實為中國第一門戶。

translations.literal: To the southeast it looks down on Kalimantan and Luzon; to the southwest it remotely controls Vietnam, Siam, Burma, and Singapore—it is truly China’s foremost gateway.
translations.idiomatic: It overlooks Kalimantan and Luzon to the southeast and commands routes to Vietnam, Siam, Burma, and Singapore—China’s foremost maritime gateway.

sentences.zh: 其地產有山木，可採以成舟航；

translations.literal: Its land produces mountain timber that can be harvested to build ships;
translations.idiomatic: Its hills yield timber for shipbuilding;

sentences.zh: 有煤鐵，可開以資製造。

translations.literal: it has coal and iron that can be opened to supply manufacture.
translations.idiomatic: its coal and iron can feed industry.

sentences.zh: 其客民多漳、泉、湖、嘉剛猛耐苦之人，足備水師之選。

translations.literal: Its sojourning people are mostly hardy, tough, and enduring men from Zhangzhou, Quanzhou, Huzhou, and Jiaxing—enough to supply selection for the navy.
translations.idiomatic: Hardy settlers from Zhangzhou, Quanzhou, Huzhou, and Jiaxing would make excellent sailors.

sentences.zh: 如得幹略大員，假以便宜，俾之輯和民、番，兼用西人機器，以取煤鐵山木之利，數年後可開製造局；

translations.literal: If a capable senior official were granted discretionary authority to reconcile settlers and aborigines, use Western machinery together with them, and take the benefits of coal, iron, and mountain timber, then within several years a manufacturing bureau could be opened;
translations.idiomatic: Appoint a capable official with broad authority to reconcile settlers and indigenous peoples, use Western machinery, and exploit coal, iron, and timber—a factory could follow in a few years;

sentences.zh: 練海師，為沿海各省聲援，絕東西各國窺伺。

translations.literal: drill a navy, serve as support for coastal provinces, and cut off the covetous glances of Eastern and Western countries.
translations.idiomatic: train a navy to support the coast and deter foreign designs.

sentences.zh: 此中國防海之要略，事之可行者一也。

translations.literal: This is the essential strategy for China’s coastal defense—the first feasible measure.
translations.idiomatic: That is the first practical step in coastal defense.

sentences.zh: 海外新嘉坡、檳榔嶼、舊金山、新金山各埠，均有閩、廣人在彼貿易，每處不下數万人。

translations.literal: At the overseas ports of Singapore, Penang, San Francisco, and Melbourne, Fujian and Guangdong people trade at each place, no fewer than tens of thousands at each.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of Fujian and Guangdong traders live at Singapore, Penang, San Francisco, and Melbourne.

sentences.zh: 其為首領者，必有幹濟之才，足以提倡全埠。

translations.literal: Among them as leaders there must be men of practical ability sufficient to uplift the whole port.
translations.idiomatic: Their leaders include men capable of organizing whole communities.

sentences.zh: 如派領事出洋，物色人才，不論官階文武大小，有能任此事者，給以虛銜，令前往各埠結納首領，婉轉勸導，由各省督撫奏給職官，派為練首，令其團練壯丁，隨時操演。

translations.literal: If consuls were dispatched abroad to seek talent, regardless of civil or military rank, great or small, and those able to undertake this were given nominal titles and sent to each port to win over leaders and persuade them gently, then through memorials by provincial governors and governor-generals official posts could be granted, appointing them as drill leaders and ordering them to organize able-bodied men and drill them at regular times—
translations.idiomatic: Send consuls to recruit leaders abroad—any capable man, civil or military—and give them nominal rank to organize and drill local militia, with provincial governors confirming appointments.

sentences.zh: 約計經費有限，而獲益無窮，事之可行者二也。

translations.literal: Estimated expenses would be limited, while the benefit would be boundless—the second feasible measure.
translations.idiomatic: Costs would be modest; the gain immense—that is the second measure.

sentences.zh: 現在通商各口，外人星羅釭布，中國情事，無一不周知，而彼都情形，中國則皆未深悉。

translations.literal: At the treaty ports now open to trade, foreigners are scattered like stars; nothing of China’s affairs is not thoroughly known to them, while on their countries’ conditions China is still not deeply informed.
translations.idiomatic: Foreigners fill every treaty port and know China inside out, while China remains poorly informed about them.

sentences.zh: 自斌椿、志剛、孫家穀出使後，至今無續往之人。

translations.literal: Since Binchun, Zhigang, and Sun Jiangu went as envoys, until now there has been no one continuing to go.
translations.idiomatic: Since the missions of Binchun, Zhigang, and Sun Jiangu, no envoys have followed.

sentences.zh: 竊謂宜選有才略而明大體者，隨時遣使，設有交涉，可辯論者與之辯論，可豫防者密為設防。

translations.literal: Your servant thinks men of talent and broad vision should be chosen and envoys sent as occasion requires; when negotiations arise, what can be argued should be argued, and what can be guarded against should secretly be guarded against.
translations.idiomatic: Choose able, broad-minded envoys as needed—to argue where argument helps and to prepare defenses in advance.

sentences.zh: 且於彼國有用之人才，新造之精器，均可隨時採訪，以為招致購買之地，事之可行者三也。」

translations.literal: Moreover, useful talent in those countries and newly made fine instruments can all be inquired into at any time as places for recruiting and purchasing—the third feasible measure."
translations.idiomatic: They could also scout foreign talent and new inventions for recruitment and purchase—the third measure.

sentences.zh: 尋乞病罷歸。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he begged leave on grounds of illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 光緒四年，東鄉民亂，命宗羲按讞。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Guangxu, there was a popular uprising in Dongxiang; Zongxi was ordered to review the cases.
translations.idiomatic: In 1878, after the Dongxiang uprising, Zongxi was ordered to review the cases.

sentences.zh: 宗羲以知縣孫定揚浮收激變，冒昧請兵，提督李有恆妄殺平民千餘，據實入告，獄獲平反。

translations.literal: Zongxi found that Magistrate Sun Dingyang’s excessive levies had provoked the revolt, that he had rashly requested troops, and that Commander Li Youheng had wantonly killed more than a thousand civilians; reporting the facts, the cases were reversed.
translations.idiomatic: He found Magistrate Sun Dingyang’s exactions had sparked the revolt, that Sun had rashly called in troops, and that Commander Li Youheng had slaughtered more than a thousand civilians; his report led to reversal of the verdicts.

sentences.zh: 六年，召詣京師，以病未癒，疏請乞緩行。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was summoned to the capital; because his illness had not healed, he memorialized asking to delay going.
translations.idiomatic: In 1880 the court summoned him to Beijing, but he asked to delay because he was still ill.

sentences.zh: 十年，卒，賜祭葬。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he died; imperial sacrifice and burial were granted.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1884; the court granted funeral honors.

sentences.zh: 子方本，舉人，兵部郎中。

translations.literal: His son Fang Ben was a provincial graduate and served as bureau director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fang Ben, a provincial graduate, served as a director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 有幹濟。

translations.literal: He had practical ability.
translations.idiomatic: He was capable and effective.

sentences.zh: 總督鹿傳霖、錫良先後令董商務、學務。

translations.literal: Governors-General Lu Chuanlin and Xi Liang successively ordered him to oversee commerce and education affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Governors-General Lu Chuanlin and Xi Liang put him in charge of commerce and education.

sentences.zh: 川東旱災，治賑，被疾，卒，贈太僕寺卿。

translations.literal: During drought disaster in eastern Sichuan he managed relief, fell ill, died, and was posthumously granted Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He died directing drought relief in eastern Sichuan and was posthumously made vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 徐宗幹，字樹人，江蘇通州人。

translations.literal: Xu Zonggan, style name Shuren, was a native of Tongzhou, Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zonggan, whose style was Shuren, came from Tongzhou in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶二十五年進士，山東即用知縣，除武城，調泰安。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Jiaqing he passed the jinshi examination, was assigned as magistrate in Shandong, was appointed to Wucheng, and was transferred to Tai’an.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi in 1820, served in Shandong at Wucheng and Tai’an.

sentences.zh: 在任十年，有政聲，遷高唐知州。

translations.literal: In ten years in office he had a reputation for good governance and was transferred to Prefect of Gaotang.
translations.idiomatic: After ten respected years as magistrate he became prefect of Gaotang.

sentences.zh: 道光十七年，濰縣教匪馬剛等作亂，從巡撫經額布剿擒之，議解省下獄候命。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Daoguang, teaching-bandit Ma Gang and others rose in revolt; following Governor Jinge he suppressed and captured them; it was proposed to send them under guard to the provincial capital to await orders.
translations.idiomatic: In 1837 he helped Governor Jinge suppress the teacher-rebel Ma Gang; officials proposed sending the prisoners to the provincial capital.

sentences.zh: 宗幹請於巡撫，即其地誅之，眾心以定。

translations.literal: Zonggan requested of the governor that they be executed on the spot; popular sentiment thereby settled.
translations.idiomatic: Zonggan persuaded the governor to execute them locally, calming the region.

sentences.zh: 遷濟寧直隸州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Jining direct-administration prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Jining prefecture.

sentences.zh: 金鄉民濬彭河，下游諸屯民聚眾沮之，毆官傷胥役，勢洶洶，宗幹馳往諭使解散。

translations.literal: When people of Jinxian dredged the Peng River, downstream garrison villagers gathered to obstruct it, beat officials and injured clerks and runners; the situation was turbulent; Zonggan rushed there and ordered them to disperse.
translations.idiomatic: When Jinxian dredged the Peng River, downstream garrison villagers rioted, beating officials and clerks; Zonggan rushed in and ordered them to disperse.

sentences.zh: 屯民出自首，大吏欲置重典，宗幹以為民畏水患，非與官敵，聚眾本沮工，毆官非本意，力爭戍為首者七人。

translations.literal: The garrison villagers came forward to surrender themselves; the high officials wished to impose heavy punishment; Zonggan held that the people feared flood disaster and were not enemies of the government—the gathering was originally to obstruct the work, and beating officials was not their intent; he strongly argued that only seven ringleaders be sentenced to frontier service.
translations.idiomatic: When the villagers surrendered, senior officials wanted harsh punishment; Zonggan argued they feared floods, not officialdom, and secured frontier service for only seven ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 署兗州知府，修滋陽河堤。

translations.literal: He acted as Prefect of Yanzhou and repaired the Ziyang River embankment.
translations.idiomatic: As acting Yanzhou prefect he repaired the Ziyang River dike.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，擢四川保寧知府，兼署川北道。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was promoted to Prefect of Baoning, Sichuan, and concurrently acted as Northern Sichuan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1842 he became Baoning prefect in Sichuan and acting northern Sichuan intendant.

sentences.zh: 擢福建汀漳龍道，屬縣有械半，案久不結。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Tingzhang-Long Circuit in Fujian; in a subordinate county there was armed strife over land, and the case long remained unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Tingzhang-Long intendant in Fujian, he inherited a long-unresolved armed land dispute in a subordinate county.

sentences.zh: 宗幹率壯勇數十人直入其村，集兩造剖其曲直，令同酒食以解之，令獻犯懲治，事遂解，一時梟悍皆斂跡。

translations.literal: Zonggan led several tens of braves straight into the village, gathered both parties to judge right and wrong, had them eat and drink together to settle matters, ordered the guilty handed over for punishment, and the affair was resolved; for a time fierce men all restrained themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Zonggan entered the village with a few dozen braves, heard both sides, feasted them to settle the feud, took the culprits for punishment, and subdued the local hard men.

sentences.zh: 總督劉韻珂密薦。

translations.literal: Governor-general Liu Yunke secretly recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-general Liu Yunke recommended him in secret.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，丁母憂去官，服闋，起授福建台灣道。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, on his mother's death he left office; after mourning he was reappointed Fujian Taiwan intendant.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his mother in 1845 he was reappointed Taiwan intendant in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，台灣匪洪恭等陷台灣、鳳山兩縣，复擾噶瑪蘭廳，宗幹督兵平之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng, Taiwan bandits Hong Gong and others took Taiwan and Fengshan counties and also disturbed Gmalan subprefecture; Zonggan directed troops and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: In 1853 Hong Gong's rebels took Taiwan and Fengshan and raided Gmalan; Zonggan's troops restored order.

sentences.zh: 四年，擢按察使，為巡撫王懿德所劾，解任。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was promoted to judicial commissioner but was impeached by Governor Wang Yide and removed.
translations.idiomatic: In 1854 he became judicial commissioner but Governor Wang Yide impeached him and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 旋召來京，命赴河南幫辦剿匪。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned to the capital and ordered to Henan to assist in suppressing bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon called to Beijing and sent to help suppress bandits in Henan.

sentences.zh: 六年，復命赴安徽。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was again ordered to Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: In 1856 he was sent again to Anhui.

sentences.zh: 七年，授浙江按察使，遷布政使，以短解甘餉降調。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed Zhejiang judicial commissioner, promoted to provincial treasurer, and demoted for short payment of Gansu tribute funds.
translations.idiomatic: In 1857 he became Zhejiang judicial commissioner and treasurer, then was demoted for short-paying Gansu tribute.

sentences.zh: 十年，江蘇團練大臣龐鍾璐請以宗幹辦理通、泰諸州縣團練。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Jiangsu militia director Pang Zhonglu asked that Zonggan manage militia in Tongzhou and Taizhou prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860 Pang Zhonglu asked him to organize militia in Tongzhou and Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，擢福建巡撫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he was promoted to governor of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 he was promoted to governor of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 三年，粵匪李世賢、汪海洋等由廣東入閩境，逼漳州，龍巖、雲霄、武平、永定、南靖、平和相繼陷，宗幹偕閩浙總督左宗棠以次剿平。

translations.literal: In the third year, Cantonese rebels Li Shixian, Wang Haiyang, and others entered Fujian from Guangdong, pressed Zhangzhou, and Longyan, Yunxiao, Wuping, Yongding, Nanjing, and Pinghe fell in turn; Zonggan with Fujian-Zhejiang governor-general Zuo Zongtang suppressed them step by step.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864 Li Shixian and Wang Haiyang invaded from Guangdong; six counties fell before Zonggan and Zuo Zongtang recovered them.

sentences.zh: 五年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1866.

sentences.zh: 宗棠偕將軍英桂奏：「宗幹循良著聞，居官廉惠得民，所至有聲。」

translations.literal: Zuo Zongtang together with General Ying Gui memorialized: "Zonggan is renowned as an upright local official, frugal and benevolent in office, winning the people; wherever he served he made a name."
translations.idiomatic: Zuo and General Ying Gui praised him as an upright, frugal official beloved by the people."

sentences.zh: 優詔褒卹，諡清惠，祀福建名宦。

translations.literal: An edict praised and condoled him; his posthumous name was Qinghui; he was enshrined among Fujian's famous officials.
translations.idiomatic: The court honored him posthumously as Qinghui and enshrined him among Fujian's model officials.

sentences.zh: 王凱泰，初名敦敏，字補帆，江蘇寶應人。

translations.literal: Wang Kaitai, original name Dunmin, style name Bufan, was a native of Baoying, Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kaitai, originally Dunmin, style Bufan, came from Baoying in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 道光三十年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year of Daoguang he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi in 1850, entered the Hanlin Academy, and became a compiler.

sentences.zh: 咸豐十年，以母喪歸。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Xianfeng he returned home on his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860 he went home to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 粵匪分犯江北，上命大理寺卿晏端書治江北團練，大學士彭蘊章薦凱泰使佐理。

translations.literal: Cantonese rebels attacked north of the Yangtze; the emperor ordered Dali Temple Minister Yan Duanshu to manage northern Jiangsu militia; Grand Secretary Peng Yunzhang recommended Kaitai to assist.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels threatened northern Jiangsu, Yan Duanshu directed militia and Peng Yunzhang recommended Kaitai as his aide.

sentences.zh: 敘勞，累加四品卿銜。

translations.literal: For merit he was repeatedly given fourth-rank ministerial rank.
translations.idiomatic: He earned repeated fourth-rank honors for his service.

sentences.zh: 同治二年，從巡撫李鴻章軍幕。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tongzhi he joined Governor Li Hongzhang's military staff.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 he joined Li Hongzhang's staff.

sentences.zh: 四年，浙江巡撫馬新貽薦調，命以道員發浙江，署糧道。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Zhejiang Governor Ma Xinyi recommended him for transfer; he was ordered to Zhejiang as circuit intendant and acted as grain commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1865 Ma Xinyi brought him to Zhejiang as circuit intendant acting grain commissioner.

sentences.zh: 曾國籓、李鴻章、馬新貽交章薦舉，五年，擢浙江按察使。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan, Li Hongzhang, and Ma Xinyi jointly recommended him; in the fifth year he was promoted to Zhejiang judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng, Li, and Ma recommended him; in 1866 he became Zhejiang judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 紹興三江閘洩山陰、會稽、蕭山三縣水入江，歲久沙積，三縣民請濬治。

translations.literal: At Shaoxing's Sanjiang sluice, water from Shanyin, Kuaiji, and Xiaoshan counties drained to the river; sand had accumulated over years and the three counties asked for dredging.
translations.idiomatic: Sand choked Shaoxing's Sanjiang sluice that drained three counties; locals sought dredging.

sentences.zh: 凱泰履勘濬治，復舊利。

translations.literal: Kaitai inspected on site and dredged, restoring former benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Kaitai dredged it and restored the old benefit.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷廣東布政使，裁陋規，省差徭，覈釐捐，丈沙田，濬城中六脈渠，增建應元書院。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to Guangdong provincial treasurer, cut improper fees, reduced corvée levies, audited lijin, surveyed sand fields, dredged the city's six main canals, and expanded Yingyuan Academy.
translations.idiomatic: As Guangdong treasurer he cut fees, audited lijin, dredged canals, and expanded Yingyuan Academy.

sentences.zh: 七年，擢福建巡撫，課吏興學，禁械鬥、火葬、溺女、淫祀舊俗，奏請撥釐金糴米二十萬石實常平倉。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was promoted to Fujian governor, urged officials and revived schools, forbade armed fights, cremation, infanticide, and improper sacrifices, and memorialized to allocate 200,000 shi of lijin grain to fill ever-normal granaries.
translations.idiomatic: As Fujian governor he revived schools, banned violent customs, and filled granaries with 200,000 shi of lijin grain.

sentences.zh: 充鄉試監臨，奏請整飭科場積弊。

translations.literal: As provincial examination superintendent he memorialized to rectify examination abuses.
translations.idiomatic: As examination superintendent he sought to clean up examination abuses.

sentences.zh: 台灣獄訟淹滯，奏請勒限清釐。

translations.literal: Taiwan cases lagged; he memorialized for deadlines to clear them.
translations.idiomatic: He set deadlines to clear Taiwan's backlog of lawsuits.

sentences.zh: 十二年，應詔陳言，略謂：「宜變通者六事：一，停捐例。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, responding to an imperial call for memorials, he said in summary: "Six matters should be changed: first, halt the sale of offices.
translations.idiomatic: In 1886 he memorialized on six reforms, beginning with halting the sale of offices.

sentences.zh: 自捐俸減折，百餘金得佐雜，千餘金得正印，即道、府亦不過三四千金。

translations.literal: Since donated salaries were discounted, over a hundred taels bought a subordinate post and over a thousand a regular post—even circuit and prefect posts cost only three or four thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Discounted purchase prices let men buy posts cheaply—from clerk to prefect for a few thousand taels.

sentences.zh: 家非素豐，人思躁進，以本求利，其弊何可勝言？

translations.literal: Families not naturally wealthy seek rash advancement, using capital for profit—what abuses can be fully told?
translations.idiomatic: Men of modest means bought offices for profit—with abuses beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 今日應以停捐為急務，以江西、湖南北、四川、廣東、福建六省釐捐年提數万，又於海關、洋稅關撥數万，似可彌京銅局捐項。

translations.literal: Halting sales should be urgent; six provinces' annual lijin transfers of tens of thousands, plus customs and maritime levies, could cover Beijing's copper-bureau donations.
translations.idiomatic: He urged stopping sales, funded by lijin and customs from six provinces.

sentences.zh: 至外省籌捐雖難周知，而福建自十年至今，收銀不過數万，他省可以類推。

translations.literal: Provincial fundraising is hard to track fully, but Fujian since the tenth year has collected only tens of thousands—other provinces may be similar.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian's decade of fundraising raised only tens of thousands—other provinces likely similar.

sentences.zh: 以涓滴之微而害吏治，得不償失，請下部覈議。

translations.literal: Harming governance for trifling sums is not worth it; please have the ministries deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: Petty revenue was not worth ruined governance—he asked the ministries to decide.

sentences.zh: 一，汰冗員。

translations.literal: Second, eliminate redundant officials.
translations.idiomatic: Second: cut redundant officials.

sentences.zh: 捐納，軍功兩途，入官者眾，部寺額外司員，少者數十，多則數百，補缺無期，徒耗旅食。

translations.literal: Purchase and military merit paths bring many into office; ministries have extra clerks, few tens or many hundreds, with no hope of appointment, wasting travel and food.
translations.idiomatic: Purchase and military paths flooded offices with unpaid expectant officials.

sentences.zh: 各省候補人員，較京中倍蓰。

translations.literal: Expectant officials in provinces exceed the capital several times over.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial expectants far outnumbered those in Beijing.

sentences.zh: 按例，各省試用佐貳雜職，視各項缺數多寡，酌留十之二。

translations.literal: By regulation, acting subordinate posts in provinces keep two-tenths according to vacancy numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations allowed keeping two-tenths of acting posts relative to vacancies.

sentences.zh: 請援照大挑知縣名次在後，暫令回籍候諮之例辦理。

translations.literal: Please follow the precedent for lower-ranked metropolitan appointees sent home to await recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: He asked lower-ranked appointees be sent home to await recommendation, as with metropolitan cases.

sentences.zh: 一，限保舉。

translations.literal: Third, limit recommendations.
translations.idiomatic: Third: limit recommendations.

sentences.zh: 軍興後保案層疊，名器極濫，捷徑良多。

translations.literal: Since the war, recommendation cases have piled up, titles are extremely abused, and shortcuts are many.
translations.idiomatic: Wartime recommendations had flooded honors and shortcuts.

sentences.zh: 請下部覈議，此後保舉只准得應升之階及應升之銜，其餘班次概予刪除。

translations.literal: Please have the ministries deliberate: hereafter recommendations may grant only ranks actually due for promotion; other grades should be deleted.
translations.idiomatic: Future recommendations should grant only ranks truly due.

sentences.zh: 至一品封典，二、三品加銜，皆不得濫請。

translations.literal: First-rank enfeoffment and second- and third-rank added titles must not be requested at will.
translations.idiomatic: Grand enfeoffments and added ranks must not be abused.

sentences.zh: 一，复廉俸。

translations.literal: Fourth, restore integrity salaries.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth: restore integrity salaries.

sentences.zh: 自咸豐間軍用浩繁，京外俸廉，分別減成，京員困苦，知縣疲累，早荷聖明鑑及。

translations.literal: Since Xianfeng, military expenses have been vast; capital and provincial integrity salaries were cut; capital officials were distressed and magistrates exhausted—the sage mind has long seen this.
translations.idiomatic: Wartime cuts to integrity salaries had impoverished officials; restoration would help probity.

sentences.zh: 今欲砥礪廉隅，似廉俸复額，亦其一端。

translations.literal: To sharpen integrity, restoring full salaries is one step.
translations.idiomatic: Full integrity salaries would help restore probity.

sentences.zh: 福建文職廉額年支十三四萬兩，計現年徵起錢糧羨耗支抵尚屬有贏，道府以下各員，似可照額全支。

translations.literal: Fujian civil integrity salaries yearly are 130–140,000 taels; current grain surcharges cover it with surplus; circuit and below could receive full pay.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian could afford full integrity pay for circuit officials and below.

sentences.zh: 請中外廉俸改復舊額，或加成支放。

translations.literal: Please restore integrity salaries at old rates at court and in the provinces, or pay at increased rates.
translations.idiomatic: He asked court and provinces to restore or increase integrity salaries.

sentences.zh: 一，重學額。

translations.literal: Fifth, value examination quotas.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth: value examination quotas.

sentences.zh: 近年鼓勵捐輸，有加廣中額學額之制。

translations.literal: In recent years encouraging donations has included expanding provincial examination quotas.
translations.idiomatic: Donations had expanded provincial examination quotas.

sentences.zh: 中額三年一試，無慮濫竽。

translations.literal: Metropolitan examinations come every three years—there is fear of filling ranks with unfit men.
translations.idiomatic: Triennial metropolitan exams risked unfit men passing through inflated quotas.

sentences.zh: 至一州一縣，士風本有不齊，乃以文理淺陋者濫廁其間，甫得一衿，包攬詞訟，武斷鄉曲，流弊不堪指數。

translations.literal: Local scholarship varies, yet shallow scholars crowd in; once they gain the robe they meddle in lawsuits and bully villages—harms beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Inflated local quotas let shallow scholars gain robes and bully villages.

sentences.zh: 請嗣後各省捐輸，只加中額，不加學額，並敕各省學臣酌覈。

translations.literal: Hereafter donations should expand only metropolitan quotas, not local quotas; provincial education commissioners should review.
translations.idiomatic: Donations should expand metropolitan quotas only; education commissioners should review.

sentences.zh: 如有不能足額，奏明立案，俟文風日上，再行如額取進。

translations.literal: If quotas cannot be filled, memorialize and record; when scholarship improves, fill quotas again.
translations.idiomatic: Unfilled quotas should be recorded until scholarship improved.

sentences.zh: 一，立練營。

translations.literal: Sixth, establish drill camps.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth: establish drill camps.

sentences.zh: 營兵皆招自本籍，月餉不足贍八口，勢必另習手藝，兼營負販。

translations.literal: Camp soldiers are recruited from home districts; monthly pay cannot feed eight mouths, so they must learn crafts and trade on the side.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers' pay could not feed families, so they took side jobs.

sentences.zh: 每逢操演，不過奉行故事。

translations.literal: When drills come they only go through the motions.
translations.idiomatic: Drills were empty ritual.

sentences.zh: 設有徵調，兼旬累月，始克成行。

translations.literal: If mobilized, it takes ten or twenty days to assemble.
translations.idiomatic: Mobilization took weeks.

sentences.zh: 兵與將不相習，兵與兵亦不相識，人各一心，安能制勝？

translations.literal: Soldiers do not know officers or each other—each his own mind—how can they win?
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers knew neither officers nor comrades—how could they fight?

sentences.zh: 近年削平禍亂，全賴湘、淮各勇。

translations.literal: In recent years pacifying turmoil has relied entirely on Hunan and Huai braves.
translations.idiomatic: Recent victories depended on Hunan and Huai volunteer armies.

sentences.zh: 國家養兵，糜帑歲數千百萬，竟不得其用，其弊實由於此。

translations.literal: The state maintains troops at tens of millions yearly yet cannot use them—the harm truly lies here.
translations.idiomatic: Millions spent on regular troops yielded nothing—the system was broken.

sentences.zh: 往年江寧克復，臣函商曾國籓，備言江寧綠營應稍變通，以現存得勝之勇，改充額兵，設營分部，一洗舊習。

translations.literal: When Jiangning was recovered, I wrote Zeng Guofan urging that Jiangning Green Standard troops should be somewhat changed, using present victorious braves to fill quota troops, establishing camps by division, washing away old habits.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiangning's recovery he urged Zeng Guofan to reform Green Standard troops with victorious braves in organized camps.

sentences.zh: 國籓未及議行，旋調直隸，即設練軍，蓋亦採用臣說。

translations.literal: Guofan had not yet deliberated when he was transferred to Zhili and then established drill troops—essentially adopting my view.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng adopted the idea in Zhili as drill troops before leaving Fujian.

sentences.zh: 左宗棠在閩浙任內，奏准減兵加餉，就餉練兵，洵為救時良策。

translations.literal: Zuo Zongtang in Fujian-Zhejiang memorialized approval to reduce troops and increase pay, drilling troops on their pay—a timely good policy.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Zongtang's reduce-troops-add-pay policy in Fujian-Zhejiang was sound.

sentences.zh: 請敕下各省督撫照減兵加餉之說，而以所減之餉加於戰兵。

translations.literal: Please order provincial governors to follow reduce-troops-add-pay and add the saved pay to combat troops.
translations.idiomatic: He asked provinces to add saved pay to combat troops.

sentences.zh: 按湘、楚營製，五百人為一營，擇地分扎，隨時互調，俾卒伍皆離原籍，不致散處市廛。

translations.literal: Following Xiang-Chu camp organization, five hundred men per camp, choosing places to station and rotating periodically so soldiers leave home districts and do not scatter in markets.
translations.idiomatic: Five-hundred-man camps, rotated postings, and no soldiers loafing in towns would follow Xiang army practice.

sentences.zh: 餉不另增，兵有實用，庶化兵為勇，而武備可恃。」

translations.literal: Pay not increased, troops truly useful—then transforming soldiers into braves and military preparedness can be relied on."
translations.idiomatic: Without extra pay, usable troops could turn soldiers into effective forces."

sentences.zh: 疏入，命下部議。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the emperor ordered the ministries to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries were ordered to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 十三年，入覲，行至蘇州，疾作，乞罷，予假治疾。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he went to audience; en route at Suzhou illness struck; he begged leave and was granted leave to treat illness.
translations.idiomatic: In 1887, en route to audience at Suzhou, he fell ill and was granted sick leave.

sentences.zh: 日本窺台灣，命凱泰力疾回任。

translations.literal: Japan eyed Taiwan; Kaitai was ordered to return to duty despite illness.
translations.idiomatic: When Japan threatened Taiwan he was ordered back despite illness.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年，移駐台灣，病劇，還福州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangxu he moved headquarters to Taiwan; illness worsened and he returned to Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1875 he moved to Taiwan, then returned to Fuzhou as illness worsened.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太子少保，諡文勤。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent; posthumous name Wenqin.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously named Wenqin, Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 郭柏廕，字遠堂，福建侯官人。

translations.literal: Guo Baiyin, style name Yuantang, was a native of Houguan, Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Baiyin, style Yuantang, came from Houguan in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 道光十二年進士，選庶吉士，授編修，遷御史、給事中。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Daoguang he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, appointed compiler, and promoted to censor and supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi in 1832, entered the Hanlin, and rose to censor and supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 出為甘肅甘涼道。

translations.literal: He went out as Gansu Ganliang circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Gansu Ganliang circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，戶部銀庫虧帑事發，柏廕為御史稽察，未糾發，奪官分償，旋授主事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, when the Revenue Ministry silver vault deficit was exposed, Baiyin as censor was to investigate but did not expose it; he was stripped and made to share compensation, then appointed principal secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In 1843 he failed to expose a Revenue Ministry vault deficit as investigating censor, was fined, then made principal secretary.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，會辦本省團練，以克廈門、防延平功，擢郎中。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng he managed Fujian militia; for capturing Xiamen and defending Yanping he was promoted to director.
translations.idiomatic: In 1853 militia service at Xiamen and Yanping won him promotion to director.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，引見，交欽差大臣曾國籓差委。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, on audience he was assigned to Imperial Commissioner Zeng Guofan's staff.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 he was assigned to Zeng Guofan's staff.

sentences.zh: 二年，授江蘇糧道，擢按察使，遷布政使，護理巡撫。

translations.literal: In the second year he was appointed Jiangsu grain commissioner, promoted to judicial commissioner, then provincial treasurer, and acted as governor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 he became Jiangsu grain commissioner, then judicial commissioner, treasurer, and acting governor.

sentences.zh: 六年，擢廣西巡撫，調湖北，仍留署江蘇巡撫。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was promoted to Guangxi governor, transferred to Hubei, but remained acting Jiangsu governor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1867 he was made Guangxi governor, moved to Hubei, but stayed acting in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 方亂時，江、浙交界槍船群聚為匪，柏廕與浙江會捕，獲其首卜小二置之法。

translations.literal: During the turmoil, gun boats gathered on the Jiangsu-Zhejiang border as bandits; Baiyin with Zhejiang jointly captured their leader Bu Xiao'er and executed him by law.
translations.idiomatic: He and Zhejiang captured gun-boat bandit leader Bu Xiao'er.

sentences.zh: 禁槍船，設牌甲，稽查約束。

translations.literal: Gun boats were forbidden; placards and baojia inspection and restraint were set up.
translations.idiomatic: Gun boats were banned and baojia inspection tightened.

sentences.zh: 是年，赴湖北任，署湖廣總督。

translations.literal: That year he took up Hubei post and acted as Huguang governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: That year he took Hubei and acted as Huguang governor-general.

sentences.zh: 各省遣散營勇，會匪蕭朝翥約黨分佈黃梅、武穴、龍坪各水次，阻截散勇，偪令從為亂。

translations.literal: As provinces discharged camp braves, secret-society member Xiao Chaoxu gathered followers at Huangmei, Wuxue, and Longping water stations to intercept discharged braves and force them to join rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Discharged braves were intercepted at Huangmei and Wuxue by Xiao Chaoxu's secret society.

sentences.zh: 柏廕遣兵往捕，其黨殺朝翥以降。

translations.literal: Baiyin sent troops to capture them; the party killed Chaoxu to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Troops were sent; the gang killed Chaoxu and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 諸縣教匪，京山吳世英、蘄水馮和義、沔陽劉維義次第擒誅。

translations.literal: Teaching-bandit cases in various counties—Jingshan Wu Shiying, Qishui Feng Heyi, Mianyang Liu Weiyi—were captured and executed in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Sect rebels in Jingshan, Qishui, and Mianyang were captured and executed.

sentences.zh: 七年，奏言：「漢口鎮華、洋雜處，散勇遊匪廁其間。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he memorialized: "Hankou is a mixed Chinese and foreign town; discharged braves and vagrants mingle there.
translations.idiomatic: In 1868 he reported Hankou's mix of foreigners, discharged braves, and vagrants.

sentences.zh: 每遇撤營，散佈謠言，句結入會。

translations.literal: Whenever camps were disbanded, rumors spread and secret-society recruitment followed.
translations.idiomatic: Camp disbandment bred rumors and secret-society recruitment.

sentences.zh: 疊經懲辦，在武漢、襄樊地方分設遣勇局，凡有在鄂散勇，均令赴局報名，僱船押送回籍，酌給川資，庶無業之徒，可歸鄉里，不至流而為匪。」

translations.literal: Repeated punishments were not enough; discharge bureaus were set up in Wuhan and Xiangyang so all discharged braves in Hubei reported, were hired boats to escort home, and given travel funds so the jobless could return home and not become bandits."
translations.idiomatic: Discharge bureaus in Wuhan and Xiangyang sent braves home with travel money."

sentences.zh: 又奏言：「淮南鹽引，楚岸為大宗。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Huainan salt quotas—Hubei's share is the main block.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged restoring Huainan salt to Hubei.

sentences.zh: 自長江被擾，運道梗阻，改用淮北票私，暫濟民食，淮南銷路遂滯。

translations.literal: Since the Yangtze was disturbed and transport blocked, north Huai ticket salt was used to supply the people temporarily while Huainan sales stagnated.
translations.idiomatic: War had blocked Huainan salt; north Huai ticket salt was a temporary substitute.

sentences.zh: 請復淮南引地，禁淮北票私，停北鹽抽課。

translations.literal: He asked to restore Huainan quota territory, forbid north Huai ticket salt, and stop north-salt levies.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to restore Huainan quotas and end north Huai ticket salt.

sentences.zh: 襄、鄖、德三府前此兼銷潞鹽，亦一律禁止。」

translations.literal: Xiangyang, Yunyang, and De'an prefectures that had also sold Lu salt should likewise be forbidden."
translations.idiomatic: Lu salt in three prefectures should also be banned.

sentences.zh: 八年，多雨大水，柏廕遣吏分道治賑。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, heavy rain and great floods; Baiyin sent officials in separate routes for relief.
translations.idiomatic: In 1869 floods brought relief teams on multiple routes.

sentences.zh: 九年，再署湖廣總督。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he again acted as Huguang governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: In 1870 he again acted as Huguang governor-general.

sentences.zh: 十年，湖南會匪陷益陽、龍陽，柏廕分兵防守進剿，獲其渠。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Hunan secret-society rebels took Yiyang and Longyang; Baiyin divided troops to defend and pursue, capturing leaders.
translations.idiomatic: In 1871 Hunan rebels took Yiyang and Longyang; he captured leaders.

sentences.zh: 十二年，以病乞罷。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he begged leave on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In 1873 he resigned for illness.

sentences.zh: 光緒十年，卒。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Guangxu he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1884.

sentences.zh: 子式昌，舉人。

translations.literal: His son Shichang was a provincial graduate.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shichang was a provincial graduate.

sentences.zh: 從軍積功，以知府發浙江。

translations.literal: For military merit he was appointed prefect in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Shichang earned prefect appointment in Zhejiang through military merit.

sentences.zh: 巡撫蔣益澧調赴廣東，署肇慶。

translations.literal: Governor Jiang Yilin transferred him to Guangdong and he acted at Zhaoqing.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Jiang Yilin sent him to Guangdong as acting prefect of Zhaoqing.

sentences.zh: 益澧罷，式昌還浙江，補台州。

translations.literal: When Yilin was dismissed, Shichang returned to Zhejiang and was appointed to Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Yilin left office he returned to Zhejiang as Taizhou prefect.

sentences.zh: 劇盜黃金滿以官吏貪酷，煽亂。

translations.literal: The fierce bandit Huang Jinman stirred trouble because officials were greedy and harsh.
translations.idiomatic: Bandit Huang Jinman rebelled in reaction to corrupt, harsh officials.

sentences.zh: 式昌扼要隘，令民自守，以嚴法繩蠹吏，蠲斥苛斂。

translations.literal: Shichang held strategic passes, had the people guard themselves, punished corrupt officials by strict law, and abolished harsh levies.
translations.idiomatic: Shichang held key passes, organized local defense, punished corrupt officials, and cut oppressive levies.

sentences.zh: 金滿乃詣彭玉麟請降。

translations.literal: Jinman then went to Peng Yulin to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Jinman then surrendered to Peng Yulin.

sentences.zh: 光緒二十六年，衢州民殺教士，戕西安知縣吳德潚。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Guangxu, Quzhou people killed missionaries and killed Xi'an magistrate Wu Deshao.
translations.idiomatic: In 1900 Quzhou people killed missionaries and murdered Xi'an magistrate Wu Deshao.

sentences.zh: 擢式昌金衢嚴道，諭士民安堵，得亂首誅之。

translations.literal: Shichang was promoted to Jinhua-Quzhou-Yanzhou circuit intendant, reassured scholars and people to stay calm, and obtained the ringleaders and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Jinhua-Quzhou-Yanzhou circuit intendant, he calmed the region and executed the ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，署按察使。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he acted as judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1905 he acted as judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 武昌子曾炘，官至禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: Wuchang son Zeng Qin rose to vice minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zeng Qin of Wuchang became vice minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 論曰：王慶雲、譚廷襄並敭歷中外，慶雲綜覈精密，治防井井，尤為可稱。

translations.literal: The critique says: Wang Qingyun and Tan Tingxiang both easily held office at court and in the provinces; Qingyun's comprehensive review was precise and his defense arrangements orderly—especially praiseworthy.
translations.idiomatic: The historians note that Wang Qingyun and Tan Tingxiang served widely at court and in the provinces; Qingyun's fiscal precision and orderly defenses were especially admirable.

sentences.zh: 馬新貽、李宗羲皆以循吏贊畫軍事，擢任大籓，治績卓著。

translations.literal: Ma Xinyi and Li Zongxi both rose from model local officials advising on military affairs to great provincial posts, with outstanding administrative records.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xinyi and Li Zongxi rose from model local officials to great provincial posts with distinguished records.

sentences.zh: 宗羲諫園工，籌海防，建言遠大。

translations.literal: Zongxi remonstrated against garden works and planned coastal defense—his counsel was far-reaching.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zongxi's protests against Yuanmingyuan rebuilding and his coastal-defense plans were far-sighted.

sentences.zh: 徐宗幹、王凱泰清節惠政，皆有時望。

translations.literal: Xu Zonggan and Wang Kaitai were known for integrity and benevolent government and enjoyed contemporary esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zonggan and Wang Kaitai were esteemed for integrity and benevolent rule.

sentences.zh: 郭柏廕久任疆圻，澤施於後焉。

translations.literal: Guo Baiyin long held frontier posts and his beneficence extended to later generations.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Baiyin's long service on the frontiers left benefits for generations after.
